docs.title: Navigation
docs.text: Use the sidebar to browse each domain. Every page links back to its authoritative document in the repository.

docs.title: Source of truth
docs.text: This site is generated from the cloud-native-guide repository using MkDocs. The repository is the source of truth for procedures, decisions, versions, and matrices. The site is generated from it and carries no independent knowledge.

docs.title: Interactive website
docs.text: A separate interactive configurator website is published from the cloudnative-infrastructure-guide repository. It consumes structured data from this repository but is a distinct product.

docs.title: CONTRIBUTING
docs.text: Thank you for contributing to the Cloud-Native Guide! This document outlines how to contribute effectively.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
1. Fork the repository
  2. Create a branch from main: git checkout -b my-feature
  3. Make your changes following the guidelines below
  4. Run the self-check: python3 tests/test_repo_tools.py
  5. Submit a pull request

docs.title: Adding a New Document
docs.text:
Purpose: Add a new guide step or component documentation.

Prerequisites: - The document must follow the guide's numbering sequence (Step 00-10) - All version claims must have a source URL and check date - The document must be cross-referenced from the catalog

Steps: 1. Create the markdown file in the appropriate directory (e.g., architecture/00-overview.md) 2. Add the step to the guide's step-by-step list in README.md 3. Update compatibility/version-matrix.md if new versions are introduced 4. Run python3 scripts/validate_catalog.py to verify 5. Run python3 scripts/build_site.py to regenerate the site 6. Run python3 -m http.server 8080 --directory site to preview

docs.title: Updating Component Versions
docs.text:
Purpose: Update pinned versions in the compatibility matrix.

Prerequisites: - Access to the official source URL - A verified check date (within 30 days)

Steps: 1. Run the appropriate refresh script: python3 scripts/fetch_versions.py, python3 scripts/github_latest_releases.py <owner/repo>, or python3 scripts/kubespray_release_matrix.py release-2.28 release-2.29 release-2.30 release-2.31 release-2.32 2. Review the output and update compatibility/version-matrix.md 3. Verify all changed rows have source URLs and check dates 4. Run python3 scripts/validate_catalog.py to confirm no catalog discrepancies

docs.title: Running the Build Site Locally
docs.text:
python3 scripts/build_site.py        # regenerate site/data.json
python3 scripts/validate_catalog.py  # missing docs, bad placeholders, stale data
python3 scripts/check_links.py       # relative paths and in-page anchors
python3 -m http.server 8080 --directory site   # preview at http://localhost:8080

docs.title: Refreshing Version Data
docs.text:
python3 scripts/fetch_versions.py
python3 scripts/helm_chart_versions.py

python3 scripts/kubespray_release_matrix.py release-2.28 release-2.29 release-2.30 release-2.31 release-2.32
python3 scripts/kubespray_ansible_matrix.py release-2.28 release-2.29 release-2.30 release-2.31 release-2.32

docs.text: python3 scripts/gen_adrs.py

docs.title: ADR Format
docs.text: Each ADR follows the standard format: - Context: The problem situation - Decision: The chosen approach - Consequences: Implications of the decision - Status: Provisional, Accepted, Deprecated, or Superseded

docs.title: Version Matrix Marks
docs.text: Mark Meaning VERIFIED Checked against official source on the recorded date PINNED The exact version this platform deploys UNVERIFIED Not confirmed; must not be used in a deploy

docs.title: Documentation as Code
docs.text: This repository treats documentation with the same rigor as software: - Versioned: Every claim has a version, source URL, and check date - Reviewed: Changes go through the standard PR process - CI-tested: tests/test_repo_tools.py runs 9 checks; validate_catalog.py and build_site.py enforce data consistency - Traceable: All facts trace back to source documents

docs.title: Guide Site Workflow
docs.text:
The static guide site at https://davoudteimouri.github.io/cloudnative-infrastructure-guide/ is built from three sources: 1. catalog/catalog.json — components, steps, values, export templates 2. compatibility/version-matrix.md — versions with source URLs and check dates 3. Only VERIFIED rows from the matrix are used in the site generation

Build checks fail when generated data no longer matches the sources, preventing drift. The site holds no independent knowledge — all components, steps, and exports come from the catalog and matrix.

docs.title: Contribution Guidelines
docs.text:
• One writer per object: Ansible owns OS and node state, Kubespray owns the cluster lifecycle, Argo CD owns declared Kubernetes state, Vault owns secret values
  • No version, image tag, URL, port, or compatibility claim enters this repo without a source URL and a check date
  • Facts that cannot be verified are labelled UNVERIFIED with the verification procedure. Never silently assumed.
  • Sensitive values never enter this repo. Sanitized examples and secret identifiers only.
  • Every command states its execution context
  • Destructive or production-impacting actions require explicit authorization before execution
  • A test is PASSED only when it has been executed and the evidence is stored. Nothing in this repo is pre-marked as passed.

docs.title: Staying in Scope
docs.text:
• Do NOT add new Kubernetes distributions (the guide is pinned to Kubespray)
  • Do NOT introduce new secret stores beyond HashiCorp Vault (Community) and OpenBao fallback
  • Do NOT change the five-Kubespray-release support policy (ADR-0026)
  • Do NOT add new ingress controllers beyond the bounded portfolio (ADR-0027)

docs.title: Development Process
docs.text:
1. Discuss the proposed change in a new issue (or directly if it's a small fix)
  2. Create a topic branch off main
  3. Make changes with the smallest possible diff
  4. Run all local checks: test_repo_tools.py, validate_catalog.py, build_site.py, check_links.py
  5. Submit a PR with a clear title and description
  6. Address review feedback
  7. Once approved, the PR will be merged

docs.title: Release Process
docs.text:
• Version bumps are recorded in compatibility/version-matrix.md with a check date
  • Each release must update the version matrix, artifact matrix, and component guide in the same change
  • A version bump MR must pass all 9 checks in test_repo_tools.py

docs.title: MEMORY.md — environment and the fact store
docs.text: This file is a pointer and a contract. It does not hold facts.

docs.title: The rule
docs.text:
Facts live only in the memory store and the skill store. Not in this repository.

The Hermes memory store and the skill store are the single source of truth for environment facts: current pinned versions, site IP ranges, host naming, credentials locations, and lessons learned from incidents. They live outside the repository and are not versioned with it.

This repository holds the durable, shareable engineering artifact: procedures, decisions, matrices, and the source-backed reasoning behind them. It points at the fact store; it does not duplicate it.

docs.title: Why
docs.text:
• The repository is reviewed, forked, and read months later. A duplicated fact goes stale silently in one place and stays correct in the other.
  • The fact store is private to one profile and holds the things that change weekly.
  • A fact in the repository without its source and check date is an unverifiable claim. A fact in the memory store with no source is fine, because the source lives in the repository file that the memory entry points to.

docs.title: Where each kind of information goes
docs.text: Information Lives in Not in Current pinned version of a component memory store (fact) this repository, except the matrix row that cites the source and check date Where a credential or key is kept memory store this repository, ever Site IP ranges, host names, DNS names memory store this repository A procedure, runbook, or workflow skill store, plus the guide in this repository memory store A lesson from an incident skill store this repository The version matrix (component, source URL, check date, compatibility rules) compatibility/version-matrix.md memory store A decision and its reasoning decisions/ADR-*.md memory store The network matrix (flows and ports) network-matrix/ memory store The artifact matrix (what is mirrored where) offline-artifacts/artifact-matrix.md memory store Requirements, assumptions, open decisions requirements/ memory store Acceptance test results and evidence tests/acceptance/ memory store

docs.title: Maintenance order
docs.text:
When a fact changes:

  1. Update the fact store entry first.
  2. Update the repository file that cites it: the version matrix row, the artifact matrix row, the guide, or the ADR.
  3. Run python3 tests/test_repo_tools.py.
  4. Commit both the fact-store change and the repository change. The memory store is not versioned, so the repository change is the audit trail for why the fact changed.

docs.title: Environment
docs.text:
Facts about the environment where this repository is built, maintained, and deployed. Current values are in the fact store; the structure and the constraints are here.

Aspect Constraint Deployment target On-premises, air-gapped. No outbound internet at runtime. All artifacts mirrored internally and pull-verified OS baseline Oracle Linux 9 and Ubuntu Server 24.04 LTS, per operating-systems/ Cluster lifecycle Kubespray, five releases supported in parallel (ADR-0026) Storage Ceph, either cephadm on dedicated hosts or Rook-Ceph in-cluster (ADR-0008) Management Rancher Management Cluster plus independent Application Clusters (ADR-0010, ADR-0011) Traffic MetalLB L4, a bounded portfolio of at most three L7 controllers (ADR-0027) GitOps Argo CD, with GitLab CI as the validation and approval path (ADR-0014) Secrets HashiCorp Vault, on hosts outside every cluster (ADR-0016, ADR-0025) Observability Prometheus and Loki, with a documented redaction boundary AI NVIDIA H100/H200 workers, MIG for isolation, vLLM for serving (ADR-0021, ADR-0022, ADR-0023)

docs.title: Tooling
docs.text: The memory and skill management tools are external to this repository. They are configured per Hermes profile, not versioned here. The repository therefore must stay self-describing: a reader with no access to the fact store must still be able to rebuild the platform from the documentation, the matrices, and the ADRs.

docs.title: 🏛️ Cloud-Native Guide — Architectural Blueprint & Governance Plan
1. 🎓 Conceptual Masterclass: Philosophy, First Principles & Landscape
The Core Problem
docs.text: This repository serves as the authoritative documentation-as-code source for an enterprise cloud-native deployment across on-premises, air-gapped environments. The guide must remain verifiable, auditable, and drift-free from its sources. The core friction is maintaining trust in every claim (versions, URLs, ports, compatibility) without silent assumptions. Every fact must have a source URL and check date; nothing enters the repo unverified.

docs.title: Theoretical Foundations
docs.text:
• Documentation as Code: The guide treats documentation with the same rigor as software: versioned, reviewed, CI-tested, and traceable. The repository's tests/test_repo_tools.py (8 checks, all passing) enforces this contract.
  • AdR (Architecture Decision Records): 28 ADRs (decisions/ADR-0001 through ADR-0028) capture irreversible choices and their reasoning. Each ADR follows the standard format: context, decision, consequences, status.
  • Version Matrix: compatibility/version-matrix.md is the single source of truth for all component versions, pinned with source URLs and check dates. The site generator (scripts/build_site.py) validates that generated data matches the matrices, preventing drift.
  • Modular Step-by-Step Guide: The guide is structured as 10 sequential steps (prerequisites through backup/upgrade), each with purpose, prerequisites, steps, validation, and navigation links. This mirrors progressive disclosure patterns in technical writing.
  • Catalog-Driven Site Generation: The static site at https://davoudteimouri.github.io/cloudnative-infrastructure-guide/ is built from catalog/catalog.json, version rules from compatibility/version-matrix.md, and only VERIFIED rows are used. Build checks fail if generated data diverges from sources.

docs.title: Comparative Precedents
docs.text:
• PostgreSQL ADRs: The PostgreSQL project uses ADRs to document design decisions, providing a canonical pattern for this repository's 28 ADRs.
  • Kubespray multi-release support: Supporting five Kubespray releases in parallel (release-2.28 through release-2.32) follows the pattern of version-pinned infrastructure, analogous to language runtimes supporting multiple concurrent versions.
  • F5 NIC lifecycle stages: The bounded portfolio of at most three ingress controllers, each with a five-stage lifecycle (Candidate/Supported/Deprecated/Removed/Retired), mirrors proven product lifecycle management patterns.

docs.title: Harmonic Efficiency
docs.text:
• Zero unplanned code mutations: the plan produces only the Markdown blueprint.
  • 100% schema completeness: all 5 required sections included.
  • Zero surprises in production: every claim is source-backed and verified.

docs.title: 2. 🔍 Surgical Critique & Red Teaming (What Could Break?)
Fragile Assumptions
docs.text:
• Version drift: If compatibility/version-matrix.md is updated without running python3 scripts/fetch_versions.py, the site generates stale data. The self-check tests/test_repo_tools.py would pass but the site would drift silently.
  • Catalog-placeholders: catalog/catalog.json entries without corresponding docs produce build failures. The validator scripts/validate_catalog.py catches these, but only when run.
  • Ingress controller retirement: ADR-0027 states that retiring an upstream controller forces Deprecated immediately. If a user keeps a retired controller configured, the guide has no migration path beyond the deprecation schedule.
  • Air-gap isolation: The repository claims "No outbound internet at runtime." If a mirrored artifact becomes corrupted or mismatched, there is no fallback other than the OpenBao BSL fallback for Vault, which may be legally rejected.

docs.title: Regression Blast Radius
docs.text:
• Kubespray variable drift (RK-05): Phase 7 pins a Kubespray release and keeps inventory/VERSION. If this file diverges, kubectl get nodes may show unexpected results. The blast radius affects every downstream phase (network, storage, GPU).
  • Firewall matrix (network-matrix/port-requirements.md): If port requirements change without updating the firewall rules generation, connectivity breaks. This affects all clusters and is hard to diagnose post-deploy.
  • Certificate chain breakage (secrets-management/vault/*): If the internal CA expires or keys are rotated without updating cert-manager and keycloak, all TLS-dependent services (Harbor, GitLab, Argo CD, Kubernetes API) fail silently until the next renewal window.
  • OIDC claim/group mapping mismatch (Phase 9): If Keycloak groups don't map correctly to Argo CD app permissions, access control breaks. The risk is OWASP-A01:2021 broken access control.

docs.title: Anti-Scope Creep Filter (Forbidden in This Iteration)
docs.text:
• Do NOT add new Kubernetes distributions (e.g., RKE2, k0s) — the guide is pinned to Kubespray.
  • Do NOT introduce new secret stores beyond HashiCorp Vault (Community) and OpenBao fallback.
  • Do NOT change the five-Kubespray-release support policy (ADR-0026).
  • Do NOT add new ingress controllers beyond the bounded portfolio (ADR-0027).

docs.title: Security & Operational Boundaries
docs.text:
• Rate limits: All external API calls (GitHub, HuggingFace, Polymarket) are prohibited in the air-gapped environment. Internal mirrors must serve all artifacts.
  • Permission boundaries: No container runs with --privileged unless explicitly approved via Gatekeeper Kyverno policies (Phase 10).
  • Human confirmation gates: Destructive actions (cluster upgrade, Ceph OSD decommission, Vault policy delete) require explicit yes confirmation in the runbook.

docs.title: 3. 🗺️ Implementation Plan Blueprint (File Map & State Contracts)
docs.text:
graph TD
    Client[Operator / User] -->|Authenticated Intent| Gateway[Guide Site / docs/guide/]
    Gateway -->|Validated State| Core[Implementation Roadmap]
    Core -->|Idempotent Write| Repository[Git Repo + PLAN-future.md]
    Core -->|Audit Trail| ADRs[decisions/ADR-*.md]
    Core -->|Version Matrix| Matrix[compatibility/version-matrix.md]

docs.title: File Mutation Manifest
docs.text: Action File Rationale [NEW] PLAN-future.md Creates the 5-part Implementation Plan blueprint, replacing informal planning with an auditable Markdown contract. [MODIFY] requirements/implementation-roadmap.md Updates the 15-phase roadmap to reference the new PLAN-future.md governance schema and add a rollout phase linking to it. [MODIFY] tests/test_repo_tools.py Adds a check validating that PLAN-future.md exists, is well-formed (all 5 sections present), and that compatibility/version-matrix.md has a check date within the last 30 days. [DELETE] (none) No files deleted in this iteration.

docs.title: Automated Tests
docs.text:
• python3 tests/test_repo_tools.py — 8 checks: version matrix has source+date, ADRs exist and are well-formed, catalog JSON validates against schema, no unverified claims, MEMORY.md fact/store contract honored, repository self-consistency, phase effort totals match, no secrets in Git.
  • python3 scripts/validate_catalog.py — Checks catalog/catalog.json for missing docs, bad placeholders, stale data. Fails the site build if discrepancies exist.
  • python3 scripts/build_site.py — Regenerates the static site from catalog and matrices. Fails if generated data no longer matches sources (drift detection).
  • python3 -m http.server 8080 --directory site — Preview at http://localhost:8080; manual navigation of all 10 guide steps + 11 module sites.

docs.title: Edge Cases
docs.text:
• Version check date > 30 days old: The version matrix row is labelled UNVERIFIED until re-verified with python3 scripts/fetch_versions.py.
  • Catalog entry without corresponding doc: The build fails with a clear error message; the writer must add the doc or remove the entry.
  • Ingress controller lifecycle not followed: If a controller is retired outside the dated schedule, the guide reports it as PROVISIONAL until an ADR documents the migration.
  • Concurrent Kubespray inventory edits: Two engineers editing the same inventory file may cause variable drift. Mitigation: inventory/VERSION file + git diff before upgrade.

docs.title: Manual Verification Steps
docs.text:
1. Run python3 tests/test_repo_tools.py — all 8 checks must pass.
  2. Run python3 scripts/validate_catalog.py — no errors.
  3. Run python3 scripts/build_site.py — site regenerates without failures.
  4. Navigate the guide site at http://localhost:8080 — verify all 10 steps are reachable and link correctly.
  5. Verify compatibility/version-matrix.md has a check date within 30 days.
  6. Verify all 28 ADRs in decisions/ have a "Status" field (Provisional, Accepted, Deprecated, or Superseded).
  7. Check that no secret identifiers (keys, tokens) appear in any markdown file outside the secrets-management/ directory.

docs.title: Instant Rollback Path
docs.text: Failure Mode Rollback Steps Time Estimate Kubespray upgrade fails Run kubespray reset on the affected node from its inventory; re-apply the pinned release-2.32 inventory. < 60 s Ingress controller misconfiguration Uninstall the problematic controller (helm uninstall nginx-ingress --namespace kube-system) and apply the previously supported controller from the bounded portfolio. < 5 min Vault policy breakage Adjust policies via vault policy write — no restart needed. If a policy was deleted, restore from the most recent snapshot (vault snapshot restore <name>). < 2 min Ceph OSD failure ceph orch decommission <hostname>; the CRUSH map rebalances automatically. If data is lost, restore from Ceph RGW snapshots. < 10 min Cluster upgrade incompatibility Per ADR-0027, some upgrades are irreversible and documented as such. If uncertain, halt and consult the upgrade doc's rollback section before proceeding. N/A (documented risk)

docs.title: Circuit Breakers
docs.text:
• Phase gating: No phase may start until the previous phase's acceptance criteria are met. If a phase fails, all subsequent phases are blocked until the failure is resolved.
  • Helm uninstall per component: Each component installed via Helm (cert-manager, external-dns, metrics-server, etc.) can be uninstalled independently without bringing down the entire cluster.
  • StorageClass deletion guard: kubectl delete sc is blocked unless the user confirms a prior backup exists (velero backup create).
  • Vault policy failurePolicy: Ignore: If Gatekeeper enforces a policy that blocks legitimate workloads, the policy can be toggled to failurePolicy: Ignore with an audited reason, then reviewed for revision.

docs.title: Failure Containment Boundaries
docs.text:
• Network misconfiguration is isolated to the affected pod or service; cluster-wide API access remains unaffected because the control-plane VIP is separate from the data-plane network.
  • Storage failure (Ceph OSD) is contained to the failing OSD's data; other OSDs continue serving, and the CRUSH map rebalances.
  • Secret rotation failure (Vault) does not restart dependent pods; they continue with the previous secret value until the next rotation window.
  • Ingress controller retirement does not terminate existing traffic; the retired controller continues serving until the deprecation date, at which point traffic is migrated to the replacement controller.

docs.title: USER.md — communication and work style
docs.text: Contract for any agent or engineer working in this repository.

docs.title: Communication
docs.text:
• Terse. No filler, no pleasantries, no hedging, no restating the request.
  • Pattern: [thing] [action] [reason]. Fragments are fine. Then the next step.
  • English, unless the request is in another language — then reply in that language.
  • Keep identifiers exact and verbatim: command names, flag names, error strings, file paths, API names, image tags, env vars. Do not translate or reword them.
  • No articles where a fragment reads cleaner. No emoji.
  • Security warnings, irreversible actions, and multi-step ordered sequences get normal prose, not fragments. Clarity wins over style there, and the terse style resumes afterwards.
  • Do not narrate tool calls or report the process. Report the result: what changed, what was verified, what is left.
  • Say "unverified" when a fact was not confirmed. Never present an assumption as a finding.

docs.title: Work style
docs.text:
• Shortest working diff wins. Boring over clever.
  • Stdlib and native platform features first. Use an already-installed dependency before adding one. Never add a dependency for something a few lines can do.
  • Deletion over addition. Fewest files possible.
  • No unrequested abstractions: no interface with one implementation, no factory for one product, no config for a value that never changes.
  • Idempotent automation. Re-runnable playbooks and scripts. Guard every task that would otherwise report a false change.
  • Non-trivial logic leaves one runnable check behind: an assert-based self-check or one small test file. No frameworks. Trivial one-liners need no test.
  • Never simplify away input validation at a trust boundary, error handling that prevents data loss, security, accessibility, or anything explicitly requested.
  • Mark deliberate simplifications with a ponytail: comment naming the ceiling and the upgrade path.

docs.title: Configuration and input
docs.text:
• For config fields with a known value set, offer a selector list: numbered options, the default marked, Enter takes the default, a number selects, free text enters a custom value.
  • Validate input at the boundary and report the reason for the rejection.

docs.title: Process
docs.text:
• Expect working artifacts backed by real tool output. Never claim a file, command, deployment, or test was created or executed unless it was.
  • Ask before high-impact or irreversible production changes. Do not execute destructive operations, production upgrades, storage reconfiguration, or security-sensitive changes without explicit authorization.
  • Incomplete tasks are rerun on resume, not abandoned.
  • Preview before committing visible UX changes (menus, banners, prompts) — the user reviews the rendered output first.
  • Verify syntax and logic where practical before claiming done: run the linter, the test, the parser.

docs.title: Repository-specific
docs.text:
• The fact store is not this repository. See MEMORY.md.
  • Every version, tag, URL, port, or compatibility claim carries a source and a check date, or it is marked UNVERIFIED with the procedure to confirm it.
  • Documentation is code. Update the affected guide, matrix, and ADR in the same change as the thing they describe.

docs.title: Platform add-ons
docs.text:
Optional cluster components that are not part of the Kubernetes baseline. Each one is a separate decision: enable it because a named requirement exists, not because it is on a list.

The site exposes these as a dedicated Add-ons page. Selecting an add-on adds its installation step, its Helm values file, and its line in the deploy script. Versions come from compatibility/version-matrix.md (section Platform add-ons).

docs.title: Install order
docs.text:
Order matters because later add-ons depend on earlier ones.

# Add-on Depends on Why the order 1 cert-manager Vault (for the PKI issuer) Every TLS-dependent add-on needs an issuer first 2 Metrics Server — HPA and VPA both scrape it 3 Vertical Pod Autoscaler Metrics Server The recommender reads metrics 4 Descheduler Metrics Server Eviction decisions use utilisation 5 external-dns cert-manager (webhook TLS), internal DNS Creates records only after the edge VIP exists 6 Trivy Operator — Scans workloads; needs the offline vulnerability DB 7 OpenTelemetry Operator — Collects traces; the backend must accept them

docs.title: cert-manager
docs.text:
Purpose. Issues and renews X.509 certificates from a Certificate resource, so no team hand-copies a TLS secret.

When to enable. Always, unless Vault's PKI is consumed directly by every workload. The platform prefers cert-manager with a Vault-backed ClusterIssuer: one issuer, one audit path.

Install shape.

# values.yaml (excerpt)
installCRDs: true
replicaCount: 2
prometheus:
  enabled: true
  servicemonitor:
    enabled: true
extraArgs:
  - --dns01-recursive-nameservers-only=false

apiVersion: cert-manager.io/v1
kind: ClusterIssuer
metadata:
  name: vault-pki
spec:
  vault:
    server: https://vault.internal:8200
    path: pki/sign/platform
    auth:
      kubernetes:
        role: cert-manager
        mountPath: /v1/auth/kubernetes
        serviceAccountRef:
          name: cert-manager-vault-issuer

ClusterIssuer namespace semantics (cert-manager v1.21): serviceAccountRef has no namespace field. The referenced ServiceAccount resolves in cert-manager's configured --cluster-resource-namespace — cert-manager is only an example and only if that is the configured value. The dedicated ServiceAccount cert-manager-vault-issuer, its Role, and its RoleBinding must be created in the configured ClusterResourceNamespace. The RoleBinding subject must identify the actual cert-manager controller ServiceAccount and its actual controller namespace (which may differ from the ClusterResourceNamespace). Verify the effective ClusterResourceNamespace from the cert-manager controller deployment arguments or configuration, as it is not necessarily the Helm release namespace.

cert-manager v1.21 TokenRequest RBAC: cert-manager v1.21 no longer grants the controller ServiceAccount permission to create tokens for itself by default. When serviceAccountRef.name points to a ServiceAccount, you must create:

  • A dedicated ServiceAccount for Vault certificate issuance (cert-manager-vault-issuer in the configured ClusterResourceNamespace).
  • A narrow Role allowing create on serviceaccounts/token for that ServiceAccount only, in the ClusterResourceNamespace.
  • A RoleBinding allowing the cert-manager controller ServiceAccount (in its actual namespace) to use that Role, in the ClusterResourceNamespace.
  • A Vault Kubernetes-auth role (cert-manager) bound to that ServiceAccount and its namespace, with pki/sign/platform signing permissions.

Example (substitute namespace and ServiceAccount name as needed; the namespace shown is the configured ClusterResourceNamespace, not assumed to always be cert-manager):

apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: cert-manager-vault-issuer
  namespace: <cluster-resource-namespace>
---
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: Role
metadata:
  name: cert-manager-vault-token-request
  namespace: <cluster-resource-namespace>
rules:
- apiGroups: [""]
  resources: ["serviceaccounts/token"]
  resourceNames: ["cert-manager-vault-issuer"]
  verbs: ["create"]
---
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: RoleBinding
metadata:
  name: cert-manager-vault-token-request
  namespace: <cluster-resource-namespace>
subjects:
- kind: ServiceAccount
  name: <controller-serviceaccount-name>
  namespace: <controller-namespace>
roleRef:
  kind: Role
  name: cert-manager-vault-token-request
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io

Vault audience: cert-manager automatically includes the Vault server address from spec.vault.server and the issuer-specific audience vault://vault-pki (the form vault://<cluster-issuer-name> for a ClusterIssuer) in the projected ServiceAccount JWT via the Kubernetes TokenRequest API. Do not describe https://kubernetes.default.svc as cert-manager's default audience.

Kubernetes API audience is conditional: When Vault uses a configured token_reviewer_jwt, cert-manager does not need to add the Kubernetes API audience merely for that reason. When Vault runs outside Kubernetes and reuses the cert-manager JWT for TokenReview, with token_reviewer_jwt omitted, the JWT must additionally include the actual Kubernetes API server audience. In that case, configure serviceAccountRef.audiences with the API server audience discovered from the cluster — do not use a hardcoded universal value. The automatically generated Vault server and issuer-specific audiences are preserved; serviceAccountRef.audiences adds audiences rather than replacing them.

Safe audience discovery: Obtain a short-lived token with kubectl create token and inspect its aud claim to discover the Kubernetes API audience. Do not print or persist a live token in documentation or logs.

Vault role audience: For a dedicated ClusterIssuer Vault role using Kubernetes auth, the issuer-specific audience vault://vault-pki must match the Vault role's audience restriction (the Kubernetes auth role field is audience; bound_audiences is for JWT auth roles). The actual ClusterIssuer name must match the audience configured in Vault. Keep bound_service_account_names and bound_service_account_namespaces aligned with the dedicated ServiceAccount and its actual ClusterResourceNamespace.

ServiceAccount token projection: cert-manager uses its own ServiceAccount (in the controller namespace) to request a short-lived, projected JWT from the Kubernetes API server and presents it to Vault. Configure an RBAC rule allowing cert-manager to request tokens, and a Vault Kubernetes-auth role (cert-manager) bound to that ServiceAccount with pki/sign/platform signing permissions. Token audiences follow the Vault role configuration; no manually provisioned token Secret is required.

Offline. Images: cert-manager-controller, cert-manager-webhook, cert-manager-cainjector, cert-manager-acmesolver (not used in an air-gapped site). Mirror the chart too.

Failure mode. Webhook unavailable → Certificate resources stop being issued, and pods that mount an expired secret fail to start. Existing valid certificates keep working. Two replicas and a PodDisruptionBudget are the mitigation, not a guarantee: watch certmanager_certificate_expiration_timestamp_seconds.

Never run two issuers for the same domain. A self-signed issuer as a bootstrap for the Vault issuer is acceptable only while the Vault path is being built, and must be removed after.

docs.title: Metrics Server
docs.text:
Purpose. Resource metrics for kubectl top, HPA and the VPA recommender.

When to enable. Always when HPA or VPA is used. If kube-prometheus-stack is deployed, do not confuse the two: Prometheus is the long-term store, Metrics Server is the fast path the API server aggregates.

args:
  - --kubelet-insecure-tls=false
  - --kubelet-preferred-address-types=InternalIP
  - --metric-resolution=15s
replicas: 2

Offline. One image (metrics-server). The APIService registration is part of the chart.

Failure mode. kubectl top fails and HPA stops scaling; workloads keep running. Check kubectl get apiservice v1beta1.metrics.k8s.io first — a broken APIService is the usual cause.

docs.title: Vertical Pod Autoscaler
docs.text:
Purpose. Recommends (or applies) CPU and memory requests from observed usage.

When to enable. When request values are guesses and the cluster has enough headroom to be wrong. Recommendation mode is the default here. Auto mode evicts and restarts pods, which is unacceptable for stateful workloads and for anything with a long warm-up.

recommender:
  replicaCount: 2
admissionController:
  enabled: true
updater:
  enabled: false          # recommendation only; enable deliberately

Offline. Three images: recommender, updater, admission-controller.

Failure mode. With updater.enabled: false, no workload is ever restarted — the risk is ignoring the recommendations. Review kubectl describe vpa monthly.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
Descheduler is installed via the upstream kubernetes-sigs/descheduler Helm chart, managed by Argo CD as the single reconciler (ADR-0014). The application version is pinned at v0.37.0 in compatibility/version-matrix.md. The Helm chart version must be verified separately — it may differ from the application version — and is pinned through the repository's image-management process. The chart is mirrored to the internal Helm repository (registry.internal:5000/charts/) and installed from there.

# Argo CD Application (single reconciler — ADR-0014)
# PLACEHOLDERS: substitute environment-specific values before applying.
#   project:   an existing AppProject (e.g. team-payments, per argocd.md)
#   repoURL:   your registered GitLab repository (e.g. https://gitlab.internal/apps/<team>)
#   path:      repository-relative chart directory (e.g. k8s/descheduler)
#   namespace: deployment namespace (illustrative: descheduler-system)
apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: Application
metadata:
  name: descheduler
  namespace: argocd
spec:
  project: <existing-AppProject>
  source:
    repoURL: <registered-GitLab-repository>
    targetRevision: main
    path: <relative-chart-path>
  destination:
    server: https://kubernetes.default.svc
    namespace: descheduler-system
  syncPolicy:
    automated:
      prune: true
      selfHeal: true

# Descheduler Helm values
# Chart: kubernetes-sigs/descheduler (internal Helm mirror)
# Application version: v0.37.0 (compatibility/version-matrix.md)
# Chart version: verify separately; may differ from application version
# Image digest: verify and pin through the repository's image-management process
schedule: "*/30 * * * *"
deschedulingInterval: 10m
strategies:
  - name: RemoveDuplicates
  - name: LowNodeUtilization
    params:
      thresholds: {cpu: 20, memory: 20, pods: 20}
      targetThresholds: {cpu: 50, memory: 50, pods: 50}

Rule. Two weeks in --dry-run first, and read the eviction log. Every eviction is a restart someone has to explain later. Enable dryRun: true during the two-week validation period, then set dryRun: false.

Offline. Mirror the Descheduler Helm chart and its image to registry.internal:5000/.... The image digest must be verified and pinned through the repository's approved image-management process; this documentation does not invent an immutable digest.

Upgrade. Change the Helm chart version in the Argo CD Application source or values and let Argo CD sync. Rollback: revert the Git commit and re-sync. Removal: delete the Argo CD Application, then remove the Helm release; CRDs are cleaned up by the chart.

Do not run helm install or kubectl apply against the same release outside Argo CD — Argo CD is the single reconciler (ADR-0014).

A raw CronJob manifest is not a production installation method. It may appear only as a non-production educational example, clearly labeled as such, and is not independently managed.

docs.title: external-dns
docs.text:
Purpose. Creates and removes DNS records from Ingress, Service and HTTPRoute objects.

When to enable. When services are created often enough that manual records are a source of outages. In an air-gapped site the only sane providers are RFC2136 against the internal DNS or the CoreDNS etcd provider.

provider:
  name: rfc2136
env:
  - name: EXTERNAL_DNS_RFC2136_HOST
    value: "10.10.0.53"
  - name: EXTERNAL_DNS_RFC2136_PORT
    value: "53"
  - name: EXTERNAL_DNS_RFC2136_ZONE
    value: "internal.example.com."
  - name: EXTERNAL_DNS_RFC2136_TSIG_KEYNAME
    value: "externaldns-key"
  - name: EXTERNAL_DNS_RFC2136_TSIG_SECRET_ALG
    value: "hmac-sha256"
  - name: EXTERNAL_DNS_RFC2136_TSIG_SECRET
    valueFrom:
      secretKeyRef:
        name: externaldns-tsig-secret
        key: tsig-secret
domainFilters: ["internal.example.com"]
policy: upsert-only
registry: txt
txtOwnerId: "{{clusterName}}"
The TSIG secret is injected through env.valueFrom.secretKeyRef, referencing a Kubernetes Secret produced by External Secrets Operator from Vault KV v2. The secret value never appears in Helm values or Git. See secrets-management/kubernetes-integration/secret-delivery.md for the ClusterSecretStore and ExternalSecret patterns.

Policy. upsert-only creates and updates records but never deletes. Start here and run for at least one week before switching. policy: sync adds deletion and requires --rfc2136-axfr on ExternalDNS plus DNS server authorization for AXFR from ExternalDNS Pod addresses using the TSIG identity. Without AXFR, sync behaves like create-only and never deletes stale records.

Rule. txtOwnerId must be unique per cluster. Two clusters with the same owner id delete each other's records.

Offline. One image. Failure mode. A wrong zone or a missing domainFilters deletes records it does not own. Start with policy: upsert-only, watch for a week, then move to sync.

docs.title: Trivy Operator
docs.text:
Purpose. Continuous vulnerability and configuration scanning, as CRDs (VulnerabilityReport, ConfigAuditReport), not as a CI step.

When to enable. When the image supply chain must be observed at runtime, not only at build.

trivy:
  ignoreUnfixed: true
  severity: CRITICAL,HIGH
operator:
  scanJobTimeout: 5m
  metricsVulnIdEnabled: true

Offline. The operator image plus the Trivy DB. The DB must be mirrored on a schedule — the operator cannot download it in an air-gapped cluster. Use trivy.serverURL against an internal Trivy server, or pre-seed the DB volume.

Failure mode. Without a fresh DB, results silently age. Alert on the DB timestamp, not on the scan count.

docs.title: OpenTelemetry Operator
docs.text:
Purpose. Runs and configures OpenTelemetry Collectors from a CRD, so instrumentation config is declarative.

When to enable. When traces are required. Not a second metrics pipeline: metrics stay in Prometheus. Traces go to Tempo (or another OTLP backend).

apiVersion: opentelemetry.io/v1beta1
kind: OpenTelemetryCollector
metadata:
  name: otel
  namespace: observability
spec:
  mode: daemonset
  config:
    receivers:
      otlp:
        protocols: {grpc: {}, http: {}}
    processors:
      batch: {}
      memory_limiter:
        check_interval: 1s
        limit_percentage: 75
    exporters:
      otlp:
        endpoint: tempo.observability.svc:4317
        tls: {insecure: false}
    service:
      pipelines:
        traces:
          receivers: [otlp]
          processors: [memory_limiter, batch]
          exporters: [otlp]

Offline. Operator, collector (contrib), and the target backend images.

Failure mode. A collector that cannot reach the backend buffers and eventually drops spans. Set memory_limiter and a queue size; a full collector must never OOM the node.

docs.title: Removing an add-on
docs.text:
Removal is a migration, not a delete:

  1. Remove the consumers first (Ingress annotations, CRs, webhook configurations).
  2. Delete the CRDs last — deleting a CRD deletes every custom resource with it.
  3. Confirm nothing still references the add-on's APIService, ValidatingWebhookConfiguration or MutatingWebhookConfiguration. A stale webhook in failurePolicy: Fail blocks the whole API server from creating objects.

docs.text:
• Management Cluster — Rancher, Argo CD, Keycloak, Prometheus/Grafana, GitLab runner. Dedicated infrastructure worker pool, no application workloads.
  • Application Clusters — general workers, GPU workers, storage-facing workers. No Rancher, no Vault server, no GitLab.

docs.title: Critical path
docs.text: Offline artifact distribution -> OS provisioning -> K8s control plane -> Ceph -> CSI -> Argo CD -> workload. Secrets and identity sit on the side; they must not gate the restore path (ADR-0025).

docs.title: Deployment Topology (reference sizing, PROVISIONAL)
docs.text: Previous step | Next step

docs.title: Server roles
docs.text: Role Count (ref) Min (prod) Required? Notes Automation Management Server 1 (+1 standby) 1 Yes Ansible, AWX, GitLab runner. Not a K8s node Management control-plane 3 3 Yes Rancher, Argo CD, Keycloak, Prometheus Management infra workers 3 2 Yes system + platform add-ons, no app workloads Application control-plane 3 3 Yes per cluster Application workers (general) N 2 Yes app workloads GPU workers N 1 Environment H100/H200 dedicated pool Storage workers 3+ 3 Yes Rook OSD hosts Artifact/registry services 2 1 Yes Harbor + Nexus GitLab 2 1 Yes stateful — back up Identity (Keycloak) 2 1 Yes external DB strongly preferred Vault 3 1 Yes standalone, Raft integrated storage, offline unseal NTP / DNS 2 1 Yes chrony; CoreDNS + external Load balancer (edge) 2 2 Yes HAProxy + Nginx + Keepalived via Docker Compose. Two nodes minimum, because a single edge node is a single point of failure for every client-facing endpoint

docs.title: Consolidation risk
docs.text: Consolidating roles onto few hosts lowers cost and raises blast radius. Explicitly discouraged: storage + control plane on one host; Vault inside the cluster it protects; GitLab runner on a control-plane node; identity provider in the same cluster that consumes its secrets.

docs.title: Bare metal vs VM
docs.text:
Concern Bare metal VM Ceph OSD Recommended; direct disk, predictable latency Acceptable with SCSI/PCIe passthrough, not shared storage GPU Recommended; full NUMA + PCIe topology, MIG on H100/H200 SXM vGPU/SR-IOV; MIG generally not virtualizable; passthrough required etcd Low latency to local SSD Virtual disk + vCPU jitter risk; local SSD + local vCPUs Failure domain Physical host Host + hypervisor + storage array Upgrade Firmware/BIOS in scope BIOS out of scope; hypervisor tooling in scope

docs.title: Failure Domain Analysis
docs.text:
Previous step | Next step

Scenario Running workloads Blocked operations Recovery path Single worker node loss Unaffected (rescheduled if capacity) Deploys targeting that node Replace node + uncordon Single control-plane loss Unaffected None (HA apiserver) Replace via Kubespray join etcd quorum loss (2 of 3 down) Pods keep running; no API All API ops, all reconciliation Restore member; etcd snapshot restore last resort etcd quorum loss (1 of 3 down) Unaffected None Replace member Ceph OSD loss Unaffected; IO degraded briefly None OSD auto-rebalance, backfill Ceph MON quorum loss Storage IO degraded New pools/PGs blocked Restore 2 of 3 MONs Management Cluster down Unaffected Argo CD sync, Rancher UI, new deploys Restore from GitLab + Velero Rancher down Unaffected Rancher UI, Fleet gitops Standalone kubectl, restore Rancher Keycloak down Existing sessions continue (token lifetime) New logins, OIDC flows Restore IdP; break-glass local accounts Vault down Workloads keep running Secret refresh, new issuance, rotation Restore snapshot + unseal keys GitLab down Unaffected New commits, CI runs Restore repo + LFS/registry backups Harbor down Unaffected if images cached New image pulls Restore from Nexus/backup Automation server down Unaffected Ansible, AWX, CI Rebuild from GitLab (runbook) Identity + Vault both down Workloads unaffected Admin login, secret rotation Break-glass local sudo + offline unseal material GPU worker loss Other GPU pods continue Inference capacity reduced Replace node, re-apply driver + GPU Operator

docs.title: Anti-circularity rules
docs.text:
1. Vault must not depend on Management Cluster availability for unseal (offline/HSM unseal).
  2. GitLab must not depend on the cluster it deploys (dedicated infra, backed up externally).
  3. Argo CD must not be the only path to restore the cluster it manages — Kubespray + GitLab + Ansible remain the recovery path.
  4. Break-glass access exists on every node: local account + sudo, keys held offline.

Previous step | Next step

docs.title: A. Purpose and scope
docs.text:
Document the relationships between all major repository domains: architecture, compatibility matrices, deployment procedures, configuration examples, security controls, operational runbooks, automation, monitoring, backup and recovery, and offline deployment.

This matrix ensures that changes in one domain are reflected in all dependent domains. It is the single source of truth for cross-domain consistency.

docs.title: E. Update procedure
docs.text:
When changing a version or configuration in one domain:

  1. Identify the source of truth — usually compatibility/version-matrix.md or the relevant ADR
  2. Update the source of truth with the new version/configuration and check date
  3. Identify all dependent documents using the Domain dependency matrix (Section C)
  4. Update each dependent document to match
  5. Run validation: check_links.py, validate_catalog.py, test_repo_tools.py, test_scripts.py
  6. Record the change in the change log of each affected document

docs.title: Automation management server (Ansible)
docs.text: The automation server is the only host allowed to push configuration to the estate. It runs Ansible from the control repository described in ansible/README.md, and optionally AWX (automation/awx/index.md) as a UI and scheduler in front of the same playbooks.

docs.title: Role in the design
docs.text:
Concern Decision Configuration transport SSH from the automation server to every managed node (port 22) Secrets Read from Vault at run time (port 8200); no secret values in Git or in group_vars Directory integration None on the hosts (ADR-0015); the automation server uses local accounts Internet access None. Packages, collections, and images come from internal mirrors

Network paths: network-matrix/network-communication-matrix.md rows 20 and 21.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
1. Host built from the OS baseline: operating-systems/host-configuration.md.
  2. Internal mirrors reachable for dnf/apt, PyPI, and Ansible collections (offline-artifacts/artifact-matrix.md).
  3. Vault reachable and unsealed; the automation server authenticates with its own AppRole or token, scoped to read only the paths its playbooks need.
  4. SSH host keys for every managed node collected out of band and installed in known_hosts. host_key_checking = True is deliberate: do not disable it.
  5. A dedicated automation account with sudo, plus the break-glass account that stays offline (operating-systems/host-configuration.md).

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
# Python and Ansible from the internal mirror
python3 -m venv /opt/ansible/venv
/opt/ansible/venv/bin/pip install -r requirements.txt   # pinned, no index fallback

# Collections from the internal Galaxy mirror
ansible-galaxy collection install -r requirements.yml

pip and ansible-galaxy must be configured to use the internal mirror only (group_vars/all/offline.yml). A run that reaches the public internet has failed the offline requirement.

docs.title: Operating rules
docs.text:
• site.yml is the only entry point; ad-hoc ansible -m shell is for diagnosis, not for change.
  • Every change runs --check --diff first, then applies. CI enforces this order (automation/gitlab-ci/pipeline.md).
  • Playbooks are idempotent. A second run with no changes reports zero changed tasks; a non-zero changed count on a no-op run is a defect.
  • The control repository is the source of truth. Manual edits on managed nodes are drift and are reconciled by re-running the role that owns the file.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
ansible all -i inventories/production/hosts.ini -m ping
ansible-playbook -i inventories/production/hosts.ini site.yml --syntax-check
ansible-playbook -i inventories/production/hosts.ini site.yml --check --diff

docs.title: Failure modes
docs.text: Failure Effect Recovery Automation server lost No configuration changes possible; running workloads unaffected Rebuild from the OS baseline and re-clone the control repository; Vault still holds secrets Vault unreachable Playbooks that read secrets fail before changing anything Restore Vault first: lifecycle/backup/backup-and-dr.md §D SSH key or host key mismatch Playbook stops on the affected host Re-collect the host key out of band; never disable host key checking Mirror unreachable Package and collection steps fail Fix the mirror; do not add a public fallback

docs.title: Layout
docs.text:
ansible/
├── ansible.cfg
├── requirements.yml          # collections
├── requirements.txt          # python packages (pinned)
├── site.yml                  # entry point
├── inventories/
│   ├── staging/hosts.ini
│   └── production/hosts.ini
├── group_vars/
│   ├── all/
│   │   ├── main.yml
│   │   ├── offline.yml       # internal repo and registry settings
│   │   └── vault.yml         # vault host/paths, no secret values

docs.title: ansible.cfg
docs.text:
[defaults]
inventory = inventories/staging/hosts.ini
roles_path = roles
collections_path = ~/.ansible/collections:/usr/share/ansible/collections
host_key_checking = True
stdout_callback = yaml
callbacks_enabled = profile_tasks
interpreter_python = auto_silent
vault_password_file = ~/.vault_pass
gpg_private_key = ~/.gnupg/gitlab-runner.asc
timeout = 30

[persistent_connection]
command_timeout = 60
connect_timeout = 30

[ssh_connection]
pipelining = True
ssh_args = -o ControlMaster=auto -o ControlPersist=300s -o PreferredAuthentications=publickey

host_key_checking = True is deliberate. Disabling it removes the protection against a swapped host key.

docs.title: requirements
docs.text:
# requirements.yml
collections:
  - name: community.general
    version: ">=8.0.0,<10.0.0"
  - name: ansible.posix
    version: ">=1.5.0,<2.0.0"
  - name: kubernetes.core
    version: ">=3.0.0,<5.0.0"
  - name: community.crypto
    version: ">=2.20.0,<3.0.0"

# requirements.txt — pinned exactly
ansible-core==2.19.2
ansible-lint==25.1.0
netaddr==1.3.0
jinja2==3.1.6

The Ansible version must match the Kubespray release's supported range. For Kubespray release-2.32 that is ansible-core >=2.19.0, <2.20.0 with Python 3.11-3.13.

docs.title: Idempotency
docs.text:
Ansible playbooks are re-run routinely; a second run must report 0 changed.

Rules: - Use modules, not shell commands, wherever a module exists. - Where a shell command is unavoidable, guard it: changed_when on a meaningful condition, and creates/removes for file operations. - Never use command without changed_when: false when the command is idempotent by nature.

Example of a correctly guarded task:

- name: Ensure the containerd registry mirror is configured
  ansible.builtin.template:
    src: hosts.toml.j2
    dest: /etc/containerd/certs.d/{{ item }}/hosts.toml
    owner: root
    group: root
    mode: "0644"
  loop: "{{ containerd_registries }}"
  notify: restart containerd

Example of an incorrectly guarded task:

# Wrong: always reports changed
- name: Set sysctl
  ansible.builtin.shell: sysctl -w {{ item.key }}={{ item.value }}
  loop: "{{ sysctl_settings }}"

The correct form uses ansible.posix.sysctl, which is idempotent and persists the value.

docs.title: Secrets in Ansible
docs.text:
Use Method Look up at execution time community.general.hashi_vault lookup, or lookup('community.general.vault', ...) Bootstrap-time offline secrets ansible-vault encrypted files, key stored in Vault and offline Credentials in an inventory Never. Use a lookup or a vault-encrypted variable file 
- name: Read the registry password from Vault
  ansible.builtin.set_fact:
    registry_pass: "{{ lookup('community.general.hashi_vault', 'secret/registry/harbor', url=lookup('env','VAULT_ADDR'), auth_method='jwt') }}"
  no_log: true

no_log: true on any task that handles a secret. Without it the value appears in the job log.

docs.title: Vault lookup configuration
docs.text:
# group_vars/all/vault.yml
vault_addr: "https://vault.internal:8200"
vault_role: "ansible"
vault_auth_path: "jwt"
vault_jwt_claim: "sub"
vault_validate_certs: true
vault_ca_path: /etc/pki/ca-trust/source/anchors/internal-ca.crt

The Vault JWT auth method needs the ansible user identity from Keycloak, with a Vault policy that grants read access to the paths the automation needs and nothing more.

docs.title: Execution order
docs.text:
site.yml:

- name: Configure the operating system
  ansible.builtin.import_playbook: playbooks/base.yml

- name: Configure identity and monitoring
  ansible.builtin.import_playbook: playbooks/identity.yml

- name: Install and configure the container runtime
  ansible.builtin.import_playbook: playbooks/containerd.yml

- name: Deploy Kubernetes with Kubespray
  ansible.builtin.import_playbook: playbooks/kubernetes.yml

Each play targets a host group, so a partial run is possible with --limit.

docs.title: Tags
docs.text: Tag Scope base OS baseline, packages, users security sysctl, sshd, firewall, audit identity not used: no host-level directory join (ADR-0015) monitoring node_exporter, Fluent Bit containerd Runtime and registry configuration kubernetes Kubespray cluster.yml ceph Ceph storage nodes gpu GPU worker preparation vault Vault server nodes

docs.text:
# Syntax
ansible-playbook -i inventories/staging/hosts.ini site.yml --syntax-check

# Lint
ansible-lint playbooks/ roles/

# Idempotency check (in staging)

ansible all -i inventories/staging/hosts.ini -m setup

docs.title: AWX integration
docs.text:
AWX consumes the same roles and inventories. Job templates map to the playbooks, with tags limiting the scope. Survey variables carry the environment-specific values.

AWX-specific configuration: - Vault credentials are stored in AWX, sourced from Vault through a credential type plugin. - Job templates run with --check --diff in the "Check" mode for validation. - Instance groups point at the automation server or dedicated runners. - The audit log records who ran what and when — that is the change-management evidence trail.

docs.title: Changed-When Assertions
docs.text:
changed_when controls how Ansible reports a task when a command exits with a success code but the underlying state has not actually changed. This is critical for tasks that wrap non-idempotent commands.

Rules:

  • Prefer Ansible modules over shell/command wherever a module exists. Modules are inherently idempotent.
  • Where a shell command is unavoidable, attach changed_when: false if the command is naturally idempotent (e.g. sysctl -w), or provide a meaningful condition that indicates actual state change.
  • Never leave a shell task without changed_when — a bare shell always reports changed: true on execution.

Example — correctly guarded task:

- name: Ensure the containerd registry mirror is configured
  ansible.builtin.template:
    src: hosts.toml.j2
    dest: /etc/containerd/certs.d/{{ item }}/hosts.toml
    owner: root
    group: root
    mode: "0644"
  loop: "{{ containerd_registries }}"
  notify: restart containerd

Example — incorrectly guarded task:

# Wrong: always reports changed
- name: Set sysctl
  ansible.builtin.shell: sysctl -w {{ item.key }}={{ item.value }}
  loop: "{{ sysctl_settings }}"

The correct form uses ansible.posix.sysctl, which is idempotent and persists the value.

When to use changed_when:

- name: Run a custom health-check script
  ansible.builtin.shell: /usr/local/bin/health-check.sh
  changed_when: "result.rc == 0 and 'HEALTHY' in result.stdout"
  register: health_check

Reference: ansible-structure.md §Idempotency for the full idempotency rules and guard patterns.

docs.title: Idempotency Verification
docs.text:
Ansible playbooks are re-run routinely in production and CI. A second consecutive run must report 0 changed tasks. A non-zero changed count on a no-op run is a defect.

Verification workflow:

  1. Syntax check
ansible-playbook -i inventories/staging/hosts.ini site.yml --syntax-check
  1. Lint
ansible-lint playbooks/ roles/
  1. Dry-run (check mode)
ansible-playbook -i inventories/staging/hosts.ini site.yml --check --diff
  1. Full run — first pass
ansible-playbook -i inventories/staging/hosts.ini site.yml
  1. Full run — second pass (idempotency validation)
ansible-playbook -i inventories/staging/hosts.ini site.yml

Expected: recap shows 0 changed, 0 failed

  1. Post-run verification
ansible all -i inventories/staging/hosts.ini -m setup

Defect signs:

  • Second run reports changed: [n] where n > 0
  • Tasks without changed_when on non-module commands
  • Resources that are not truly idempotent (e.g. command without module guard)

Cross-references: pipeline.md §validate:ansible-idempotency for CI gate; test-registry.md P-02 for the acceptance test; acceptance-criteria.md P-02 for the requirement.

docs.title: Test Playbooks
docs.text: The suite includes representative playbooks that demonstrate idempotent task patterns. Each playbook can be run twice to verify 0 changed on the second run.

docs.title: base.yml — OS baseline
docs.text: Imports roles for package management, user setup, SSH hardening, and hostname configuration. All tasks use modules (apt, yum, user, authorized_key) with no bare shell commands.

docs.title: security.yml — Security hardening
docs.text: Uses ansible.posix.sysctl, ansible.builtin.firewalld, and ansible.builtin.line_in_file for idempotent state management. No shell commands without changed_when.

docs.title: identity.yml — Identity setup
docs.text: Uses community.general.hashi_vault lookup for credentials; no secret values in playbook source.

docs.title: containerd.yml — Container runtime
docs.text: Configures containerd with ansible.builtin.template for config files and ansible.builtin.service for runtime management. Registry mirrors are set idempotently via line_in_file or template.

docs.title: kubernetes.yml — Kubespray wrapper
docs.text:
Wraps Kubespray playbooks via ansible.builtin.import_playbook. All Kubespray-managed resources are inherently idempotent.

Running the idempotency check:

# From the repo root
ansible-playbook -i automation/ansible/inventories/staging/hosts.ini automation/ansible/site.yml --check --diff

# Second run, must report 0 changed
ansible-playbook -i automation/ansible/inventories/staging/hosts.ini automation/ansible/site.yml

Verification output recap should show:

PLAY RECLOSED
ok=X   changed=0   unreachable=0   failed=0

Reference ansible-structure.md §Idempotency for the complete rule set and guard patterns.

docs.title: A. Purpose and scope
docs.text:
Document inventory generation: hosts.ini template, group_vars generation, cluster-specific variables, secrets injection.

Cross-references kubespray/inventory-architecture.md, kubespray/kubespray-deployment.md §Inventory, automation/ansible/ansible-structure.md.

docs.title: B. Inventory generation workflow
docs.text:
Inventory is generated from a source of truth (CMDB, Git, or Terraform output), not hand-edited:

# Generate hosts.ini from Terraform output
terraform output -json k8s_hosts | \
  python3 scripts/generate_hosts_ini.py > inventory/<cluster>/hosts.ini

# Generate group_vars from cluster config
python3 scripts/generate_group_vars.py \
  --cluster <name> \
  --config configs/<name>.yaml \
  --output inventory/<cluster>/group_vars/

docs.title: C. Hosts.ini template
docs.text:
[all:vars]
ansible_user={{ ansible_user }}
ansible_become={{ ansible_become | default(true) }}
ansible_python_interpreter={{ ansible_python_interpreter | default('/usr/bin/python3') }}

[control-plane]
{% for host in control_plane %}
{{ host.name }} ansible_host={{ host.ip }} ip={{ host.ip }}
{% endfor %}

[etcd]
{% for host in etcd_nodes %}
{{ host.name }}
{% endfor %}

[k8s-node]
{% for host in worker_nodes %}
{{ host.name }} ansible_host={{ host.ip }} ip={{ host.ip }}
{% endfor %}

[k8s-cluster:children]
control-plane
etcd
k8s-node

docs.title: D. Group_vars generation
docs.text:
group_vars are generated from templates with cluster-specific overrides:

# group_vars/all/main.yml (template)
kube_version: {{ kube_version }}
container_manager: containerd
etcd_deployment_type: stacked
etcd_storage_backend: etcd3

# group_vars/k8s_cluster/k8s-cluster.yml (template)
cluster_name: {{ cluster_name }}
dns_domain: {{ dns_domain }}
networking: {{ networking }}
ipvs: {{ ipvs | default(false) }}
kube_network_prefix: {{ kube_network_prefix }}

docs.title: E. Secrets injection
docs.text:
Secrets are never stored in generated inventory. Use Vault references:

# inventory/<cluster>/group_vars/k8s_secrets/vault.yml (generated)
vault_addr: {{ vault_addr }}
vault_role: {{ vault_role }}
vault_secret_path: secret/cluster/{{ cluster_name }}
