  • architecture/03-failure-domains.md — Control-plane node placement

This runbook is maintained as part of the cloud-native-guide. Last updated: $(date +%Y-%m-%d). For questions or updates, open an issue or submit a pull request.

docs.title: Air-gapped deployment
docs.text: Previous step | Next step

docs.title: A. Purpose and scope
docs.text:
Air-gapped = zero egress from any node at any stage. All artifacts are mirrored to internal infrastructure before any node is installed.

Artifact type Mirror target Tool Container images Internal OCI registry (Harbor/Nexus/OCI) skopeo, crane, oras OS packages (yum/apt) Internal package mirror reposync, apt-mirror, pulp Helm charts Internal Helm repo (ChartMuseum/Harbor/OCI) helm pull, helm push Binaries (kubectl, helm, cephadm, etc.) Internal HTTP file server rsync, wget Kubespray Ansible collections Internal Ansible Galaxy / collection dir ansible-galaxy collection install

docs.title: B. Air-gap workstation (the "mirror station")
docs.text: A single internet-connected workstation runs the mirroring scripts, then artifacts are transferred via sneakernet (encrypted USB, signed ISO) to the air-gapped site.

docs.title: Workstation requirements
docs.text:
• Linux (Ubuntu 24.04 / OL9 / Rocky 9)
  • ~500 GB free disk for full mirror
  • skopeo, helm, crane, oras, reposync, createrepo_c, apt-mirror installed
  • GPG key for signing mirrors (optional but recommended)

docs.title: Mirroring procedure (run on workstation)
docs.text:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# mirror-all.sh — run on the air-gap workstation
set -euo pipefail

MIRROR_DIR="/mnt/mirror"
REGISTRY="registry.internal:5000"
HELM_REPO="chartmuseum.internal"

mkdir -p "$MIRROR_DIR"/{images,packages,charts,binaries}

# 1. Container images — from compatibility/version-matrix.md
# Kubespray images
skopeo copy --all docker://quay.io/kubespray/kubespray:v2.32.0 \
  docker://$REGISTRY/kubespray/kubespray:v2.32.0
# Kubernetes control plane images (kubeadm pulls these)
skopeo copy --all docker://registry.k8s.io/kube-apiserver:v1.36.5 \
  docker://$REGISTRY/k8s/kube-apiserver:v1.36.5
skopeo copy --all docker://registry.k8s.io/kube-controller-manager:v1.36.5 \
  docker://$REGISTRY/k8s/kube-controller-manager:v1.36.5
skopeo copy --all docker://registry.k8s.io/kube-scheduler:v1.36.5 \
  docker://$REGISTRY/k8s/kube-scheduler:v1.36.5
skopeo copy --all docker://registry.k8s.io/kube-proxy:v1.36.5 \
  docker://$REGISTRY/k8s/kube-proxy:v1.36.5
skopeo copy --all docker://registry.k8s.io/etcd:3.6.15 \
  docker://$REGISTRY/k8s/etcd:3.6.15
skopeo copy --all docker://registry.k8s.io/pause:3.10 \
  docker://$REGISTRY/k8s/pause:3.10
skopeo copy --all docker://registry.k8s.io/coredns/coredns:v1.14.2 \
  docker://$REGISTRY/k8s/coredns:v1.14.2
# CNI images
skopeo copy --all docker://quay.io/cilium/cilium:v1.20.3 \
  docker://$REGISTRY/cilium/cilium:v1.20.3
# Add-ons (MetalLB, Ingress, Cert-manager, etc.) — see version-matrix.md
# Ceph images
skopeo copy --all docker://quay.io/ceph/ceph:v20.2.4 \
  docker://$REGISTRY/ceph/ceph:v20.2.4
# Rook
skopeo copy --all docker://rook/ceph:v1.21.0 \
  docker://$REGISTRY/rook/ceph:v1.21.0
# GPU Operator
skopeo copy --all docker://nvcr.io/nvidia/gpu-operator:v26.7.2 \
  docker://$REGISTRY/nvidia/gpu-operator:v26.7.2

# 2. OS packages
# Ubuntu 24.04 (for cloud-init nodes)
apt-mirror /etc/apt/mirror.list  # mirror.list points to internal mirror
# Oracle Linux 9 / Rocky 9
reposync --repoid=baseos --repoid=appstream --repoid=epel \
  --download-metadata --download-path="$MIRROR_DIR/packages/ol9"
createrepo_c "$MIRROR_DIR/packages/ol9"

# 3. Helm charts
for chart in \
  cilium/cilium-1.20.3.tgz \
  metallb/metallb-0.16.1.tgz \
  nginx-stable/nginx-ingress-2.8.0.tgz \
  jetstack/cert-manager-v1.21.2.tgz \
  rook-release/rook-ceph-1.21.0.tgz \
  prometheus-community/kube-prometheus-stack-92.11.0.tgz \
  grafana/loki-distributed-7.5.0.tgz; do
  helm pull $chart --destination "$MIRROR_DIR/charts"
done
# Push to internal ChartMuseum
for f in "$MIRROR_DIR/charts"/*.tgz; do
  curl --data-binary "@$f" https://$HELM_REPO/api/charts
done

# 4. Binaries (kubectl, kubeadm, kubelet, helm, crictl, cephadm, talosctl, etc.)
# Download from official sources, place in $MIRROR_DIR/binaries/
# Verify checksums against official releases

# 5. Package and sign
tar -czf /mnt/usb/airgap-mirror-$(date +%Y%m%d).tar.gz -C "$MIRROR_DIR" .
# Optional: gpg --sign --detach-sign /mnt/usb/airgap-mirror-*.tar.gz

docs.title: C. Site-side infrastructure (inside the air gap)
1. Internal container registry
docs.text:
# Harbor / Nexus / plain OCI registry on registry.internal:5000
# TLS certs trusted by all nodes (ca-bundle in /etc/containerd/certs.d/)

docs.title: 2. Internal package mirror
docs.text:
# NGINX serving /var/www/html/packages/
# repo files on nodes point to http://mirror.internal/packages/ol9

docs.title: 3. Internal Helm repository
docs.text:
# ChartMuseum or Harbor Helm repo at chartmuseum.internal
# helm repo add internal https://chartmuseum.internal

docs.title: 4. Internal binary server
docs.text:
# NGINX serving /var/www/html/binaries/
# Nodes fetch: wget https://binaries.internal/kubectl-v1.36.5

docs.title: Containerd config (all nodes)
docs.text:
# /etc/containerd/config.toml
[plugins."io.containerd.grpc.v1.cri".registry.mirrors."registry.k8s.io"]
  endpoint = ["https://registry.internal:5000"]
[plugins."io.containerd.grpc.v1.cri".registry.mirrors."quay.io"]
  endpoint = ["https://registry.internal:5000"]
[plugins."io.containerd.grpc.v1.cri".registry.mirrors."docker.io"]
  endpoint = ["https://registry.internal:5000"]
[plugins."io.containerd.grpc.v1.cri".registry.configs."registry.internal:5000".tls]
  ca_file = "/etc/containerd/certs.d/registry.internal:5000/ca.crt"

docs.title: Kubeadm/Kubespray config
docs.text:
# kubespray group_vars/all/offline.yml
containerd_registry_mirrors:
  registry.k8s.io: "https://registry.internal:5000"
  quay.io: "https://registry.internal:5000"
  docker.io: "https://registry.internal:5000"
containerd_registry_configs:
  "registry.internal:5000":
    tls:
      ca_file: "/etc/containerd/certs.d/registry.internal:5000/ca.crt"

# kubespray group_vars/k8s_cluster/k8s-cluster.yml
kube_image_repo: "registry.internal:5000/k8s"
kube_version: "v1.36.5"
etcd_version: "3.6.15"
containerd_version: "2.3.7"
cilium_version: "1.20.3"

docs.title: Helm values (example)
docs.text:
# values-airgap.yaml
global:
  imageRegistry: registry.internal:5000
  imagePullSecrets: [internal-registry-secret]

cilium:
  image:
    repository: registry.internal:5000/cilium/cilium
    tag: v1.20.3

metallb:
  controller:
    image:
      repository: registry.internal:5000/metallb/controller
      tag: v0.16.1
  speaker:
    image:
      repository: registry.internal:5000/metallb/speaker
      tag: v0.16.1

docs.title: E. Deployment inside the air gap
1. Transfer mirror to site
docs.text:
# On site admin host (after sneakernet transfer)
tar -xzf airgap-mirror-20261028.tar.gz -C /opt/airgap-mirror

docs.title: 2. Configure local registry as source
docs.text:
# On admin host
export CONTAINER_REGISTRY=registry.internal:5000
export HELM_REPO=https://chartmuseum.internal

docs.title: 3. Run bundle + deploy
docs.text:
# From guide repo (cloned to air-gapped admin host via sneakernet)
python3 scripts/bundle.py --answers answers/example.json --out dist/
cd dist
./deploy.sh --dry-run
./deploy.sh

The deploy.sh generated by the bundle uses: - kubespray with offline.yml pointing to internal registry - helm with --repo https://chartmuseum.internal - cephadm bootstrap --image registry.internal:5000/ceph/ceph:v20.2.4

docs.title: F. Version matrix
docs.text:
This method uses the same Kubespray releases as the standard Kubespray path. All versions are pinned in compatibility/version-matrix.md and must be mirrored exactly. See the "Kubespray → Kubernetes / etcd" and "Ceph → MON / OSD / Engine" matrices on the Deployment page.

Component Pinned version (example) Mirror location Kubespray v2.32.0 registry.internal:5000/kubespray/kubespray:v2.32.0 Kubernetes v1.36.5 registry.internal:5000/k8s/... etcd 3.6.15 registry.internal:5000/k8s/etcd:3.6.15 containerd 2.3.7 packages/ol9/containerd-2.3.7.rpm Cilium 1.20.3 chartmuseum.internal/cilium-1.20.3.tgz Ceph 20.2.4 registry.internal:5000/ceph/ceph:v20.2.4 Rook v1.21.0 registry.internal:5000/rook/ceph:v1.21.0

docs.title: G. Ongoing operations in air gap
docs.text: Operation Procedure Cluster upgrade 1. Mirror new versions on workstation 2. Transfer 3. Update kubesprayRelease in answers 4. Re-run bundle + deploy Add node Same as "Existing cluster expansion" — node prep uses internal mirrors only Ceph upgrade Mirror new Ceph image, update cephImage in answers, run cephadm upgrade Security patch Mirror patched images/packages, transfer, rolling restart via kubespray/helm

docs.title: H. Validation checklist (before declaring air gap operational)
docs.text:
• [ ] All container images pulled from registry.internal:5000 (no external pulls in logs)
  • [ ] All OS packages installed from mirror.internal (no external repos in /etc/yum.repos.d/ or /etc/apt/sources.list.d/)
  • [ ] All Helm charts deployed from chartmuseum.internal
  • [ ] All binaries fetched from binaries.internal
  • [ ] kubectl version, helm version, cephadm --version work offline
  • [ ] deploy.sh --dry-run completes with zero external connections

Source of truth: This document + compatibility/version-matrix.md + scripts/mirror_all.py (to be created) + guide bundle scripts.

docs.title: 📋 Purpose
docs.text: Document the complete offline deployment procedure for Kubespray in air-gapped environments. This procedure covers image mirroring, OS package preparation, bootstrap validation, and end-to-end installation — enabling Kubernetes cluster deployment without any outbound internet access.

docs.title: Internal Services Required
docs.text:
| Service | Description | Configuration |

|---|---|---|

| Container Image Registry | Harbor or compatible registry containing all Kubespray-required images | registry_host variable |

| OS Package Repository | Yum (RHEL/Oracle Linux) or Debian/Ubuntu repository with required OS packages | yum_repo / debian_repo / ubuntu_repo |

| Static Files Mirror | HTTP reverse proxy/cache serving binaries, zips, and helm charts | files_repo variable |

| Optional: PyPI/Helm Registries | Internal Python and Helm package registries | pypi_repo / helm_repo |

docs.title: Repository Path Mapping
docs.text:
Preserve upstream repository paths in the internal registry to minimize variable overrides:

# group_vars/all/offline.yml

registry_host: "harbor.internal"

files_repo: "http://files-repo.internal"

yum_repo: "http://yum-repo.internal"

debian_repo: "http://deb-repo.internal"

ubuntu_repo: "http://ubuntu-repo.internal"

docs.title: Step 1: Generate Image List
docs.text:
In a connected environment, generate the complete image list using Kubespray's offline tooling:

# Clone the pinned Kubespray release

git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kubespray.git

cd kubespray

git checkout release-2.32  # or pinned version from kubespray/VERSION



# Generate the image list

cd contrib/offline

./generate_list.sh

Output files:

  • temp/files.list.template — static files (binaries, zips)

  • temp/images.list.template — all container images including kube-apiserver, kube-controller-manager, kube-scheduler, kube-proxy

docs.title: Step 2: Mirror Images to Internal Registry
docs.text:
Pull each image from upstream and push to the internal registry:

# Example: Mirror control plane images

skopeo copy --dest-daemon=false \

  docker://k8s.gcr.io/kube-apiserver:v1.31.0 \

  docker://harbor.internal/k8s-tools/kube-apiserver:v1.31.0



skopey copy --dest-daemon=false \

  docker://k8s.gcr.io/kube-controller-manager:v1.31.0 \

  docker://harbor.internal/k8s-tools/kube-controller-manager:v1.31.0



skopeo copy --dest-daemon=false \

  docker://k8s.gcr.io/kube-scheduler:v1.31.0 \

  docker://harbor.internal/k8s-tools/kube-scheduler:v1.31.0



skopeo copy --dest-daemon=false \

  docker://k8s.gcr.io/kube-proxy:v1.31.0 \

  docker://harbor.internal/k8s-tools/kube-proxy:v1.31.0

Mirror all images from the generated list:

while read -r image tag; do

  skopeo copy --dest-daemon=false \

    "docker://${image}:${tag}" \

    "docker://${registry_host}/${image}:${tag}"

done < temp/images.list.template

docs.title: Step 3: Verify Image Mirroring
docs.text:
Pull test from the offline environment:

# Verify each critical image is pullable without internet access

crictl image pull ${registry_host}/kube-apiserver:v1.31.0

crictl image pull ${registry_host}/kube-proxy:v1.31.0

docs.title: Step 1: Create OS Package Repository
docs.text:
For RHEL/Oracle Linux:

# Generate repository metadata

createrepo_c ${yum_repo}/base

createrepo_c ${yum_repo}/containerd



# Required packages containerd and dependencies

# Mirror these from the connected environment:

# - containerd package and GPG key

# - Kubernetes packages (kubelet, kubectl, kubeadm)

# - Any site-specific RPMs

For Debian/Ubuntu:

# Create apt repository

apt-mirror ${debian_repo} \

  or manually construct /etc/apt/sources.list.d/internal.list



# Include required pockets

deb https://${debian_repo}/ focal main restricted

deb https://${debian_repo}/ focal-updates main restricted

deb https://${debian_repo}/ focal-security main restricted

docs.title: Step 2: Configure Package Repositories on Target Nodes
docs.text:
** containerd RHEL configuration (group_vars/all/offline.yml):**

# Oracle Linux / RHEL family

containerd_rh_repo_base_url: "${yum_repo}/containerd"

containerd_rh_repo_gpgkey: "${yum_repo}/containerd/gpg"



# Ubuntu

containerd_ubuntu_repo_base_url: "${ubuntu_repo}/containerd"

containerd_ubuntu_repo_gpgkey: "${ubuntu_repo}/containerd/gpg"

containerd_ubuntu_repo_repokey: 'YOURREPOKEY'

Kubespray group variables:

# group_vars/k8s_cluster/k8s-cluster.yml

containerd_rh_repo_base_url: "${yum_repo}/containerd"

kube_pods_subnet: "10.30.0.0/16"

kube_service_addresses: "10.32.0.0/16"

docs.title: Step 3: Verify OS Package Availability
docs.text:
# On a target node with no internet access:

yum install -y containerd.io-1.7.x  # RHEL/Oracle Linux

# or

apt-get update && apt-get install -y containerd  # Debian/Ubuntu

docs.title: Pre-Check Checklist
docs.text:
Run these validations before starting the Ansible deployment:

# 1. Verify inventory file exists and is valid

ls -la inventory/<cluster>/hosts.ini



# 2. Verify group vars are configured

ls -la inventory/<cluster>/group_vars/



# 3. Test connectivity to all nodes

ansible -i inventory/<cluster>/hosts.ini all -m ping



# 4. Syntax check the playbook

ansible-playbook -i inventory/<cluster>/hosts.ini cluster.yml --syntax-check



# 5. Dry-run limited to control-plane nodes

ansible-playbook -i inventory/<cluster>/hosts.ini cluster.yml \

  -b --check --diff --limit control-plane



# 6. Verify containerd is running on all nodes

ansible -i inventory/<cluster>/hosts.ini all -a "containerd --version"



# 7. Verify Docker/containerd registry configuration

ansible -i inventory/<cluster>/hosts.ini all -a "cat /etc/containerd/config.toml 2>/dev/null || cat /etc/containerd/config.toml"

docs.title: Expected Validation Results
docs.text:
• All nodes respond to Ansible ping

  • Playbook syntax is valid

  • containerd configuration points to internal registry

  • OS packages are installable from internal repositories

  • All required container images are available locally

docs.title: Step 1: Preparation
docs.text:
# From the Automation Management Server or bastion host



# 1. Set up the Kubespray directory with pinned release

git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/kubespray.git

cd kubespray

echo "release-2.32" > VERSION  # or pinned version



# 2. Copy the generated inventory

cp -r /path/to/generated/inventory inventory/mycluster



# 3. Verify offline group vars are in place

ls inventory/mycluster/group_vars/all/offline.yml

ls inventory/mycluster/group_vars/all/main.yml

docs.title: Step 2: Pre-Deployment Checks
docs.text:
# Run pre-deployment validation

cd /workspace/project/github/public-repository/cloud-native-guide.phase6/kubespray



# Check inventory validity

ansible -i inventory/mycluster/hosts.ini all -m ping



# Syntax check

ansible-playbook -i inventory/mycluster/hosts.ini cluster.yml --syntax-check



# Limited check on control-plane

ansible-playbook -i inventory/mycluster/hosts.ini cluster.yml \

  -b --check --diff --limit control-plane

docs.title: Step 3: Deploy the Cluster
docs.text:
# Execute the full deployment

ansible-playbook -i inventory/mycluster/hosts.ini cluster.yml -b



# Expected output phases:

# - Pre-flight checks

# - containerd setup and configuration

# - Kubernetes components installation

# - CNI (Cilium) installation

# - CoreDNS and kube-proxy setup

# - Cluster add-ons configuration

docs.title: Step 4: Post-Deployment Validation
docs.text:
# Verify cluster status

kubectl get nodes -o wide



# Verify all pods are running

kubectl get pods -A



# Verify control plane health

kubectl get --raw='/readyz?verbose'



# Verify etcd health

etcdctl --endpoints=https://127.0.0.1:2379 \

  endpoint health \

  --cacert=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/ca.crt \

  --cert=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/healthcheck-client.crt \

  --key=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/healthcheck-client.key

docs.title: Step 5: Idempotency and Reruns
docs.text:
Kubespray is idempotent by design. Reruns are safe and are the normal way to apply corrected variables:

# Rerun with updated variables

ansible-playbook -i inventory/mycluster/hosts.ini cluster.yml -b



# Add or remove workers

# - Add worker: Add to k8s-node in hosts.ini, run cluster.yml --limit <host>

# - Remove worker: drain, remove from inventory, run cluster.yml --limit <host>

# - Replace worker: drain + remove + rebuild via Ansible + re-add

docs.title: Step 6: Reset a Node (if needed)
docs.text:
# Teardown a node while preserving cluster state

ansible-playbook -i inventory/mycluster/hosts.ini reset.yml --limit <host>

docs.title: 🔄 Offline Deployment Workflow Summary
docs.text:
flowchart TD

    A[Generate image list in connected env] --> B[Mirror images to internal registry]

    B --> C[Create OS package repository]

    C --> D[Configure containerd registry mirrors]

    D --> E[Validate bootstrap (ping, syntax-check, --check)]

    E --> F[Deploy cluster with ansible-playbook]

    F --> G[Post-deployment validation]

    G --> H{All checks pass?}

    H -->|Yes| I[Cluster operational]

    H -->|No| J[Fix issues, rerun]

    J --> F

docs.title: 📦 Artifact Matrix Reference
docs.text:
Maintain artifact accountability in offline-artifacts/artifact-matrix.md. Track per-component:

| Component | Upstream Source | Internal Mirror | Mirror Status | Last Verified |

|---|---|---|---|---|

| kube-apiserver | k8s.gcr.io | harbor.internal | ✅ verified | 2026-11-26 |

| kube-controller-manager | k8s.gcr.io | harbor.internal | ✅ verified | 2026-11-26 |

| kube-scheduler | k8s.gcr.io | harbor.internal | ✅ verified | 2026-11-26 |

| kube-proxy | k8s.gcr.io | harbor.internal | ✅ verified | 2026-11-26 |

| containerd | upstream | yum/repo / apt-repo | ✅ verified | 2026-11-26 |

| Cilium Helm chart | Cilium repo | files_repo/helm.cilium.io | ✅ verified | 2026-11-26 |

docs.title: 🛠️ Troubleshooting Common Issues
docs.text:
| Symptom | Likely Cause | Resolution |

|---|---|---|

| image pull error: EOF | Image not mirrored to internal registry | Verify skopeo copy completed for all images; run pull test |

| yum/dnf error: repomd cannot be fetched | OS package repo not accessible | Check yum_repo/debian_repo URL; verify repository metadata |

| cannot connect to registry | TLS/config issue in containerd | Verify /etc/containerd/certs.d/ configuration; check containerd_registries_mirrors |

| ansible ping timeout | Network connectivity issue | Verify SSH access; check firewall rules between bastion and nodes |

| syntax error in playbook | Incompatible Kubespray version with inventory | Pin kubespray/VERSION to match inventory release |

| etcd member unhealthy | Disk pressure or misconfiguration | Check etcd disk usage; verify member addition/removal procedure |

Document generated: 2026-11-26 | Environment: Air-gapped deployment | Kubespray version: release-2.32 (pinned via kubespray/VERSION) | Registry: harbor.internal (internal image registry) | OS: Oracle Linux 9 / Ubuntu 22.04 (per inventory configuration)

docs.title: Bare-metal cloud-init / Kickstart deployment
docs.text: Previous step | Next step

docs.title: A. Purpose and scope
docs.text:
This document describes a fully automated bare-metal provisioning pipeline using cloud-init (for Ubuntu/Debian) or Kickstart (for RHEL/AlmaLinux/Rocky). The OS baseline, host tuning, and Kubespray inventory are generated from the same answers in this guide — no manual OS install step remains.

The pipeline:

  1. PXE boot (Kickstart) or cloud-init user-data (cloud-init) from an internal mirror
  2. OS baseline applied via cloud-init/Kickstart + automation/ansible playbooks
  3. Kubespray inventory generated by the guide's bundle scripts
  4. Kubespray run deploys the Kubernetes cluster

docs.title: Internal infrastructure
docs.text: Component Purpose Internal HTTP mirror Hosts OS images (cloud-init) or Kickstart trees + packages DHCP + TFTP/HTTP PXE server Serves bootloaders and Kickstart configs for Kickstart path Cloud-init user-data endpoint Internal web server serving user-data/meta-data for cloud-init path IPMI/BMC access Power control, serial console, virtual media for bare-metal nodes Container registry (Harbor/Nexus/OCI) Mirrored container images for Kubespray and add-ons OS package mirror (yum/apt) Base OS packages and Kubespray dependencies

docs.title: Node requirements
docs.text: Requirement cloud-init (Ubuntu) Kickstart (RHEL/Alma/Rocky) Boot method cloud-init NoCloud datasource (HTTP) PXE boot with Kickstart config Image cloud-init enabled Ubuntu/Debian image Minimal install ISO + Kickstart tree Network DHCP → static IP via user-data DHCP → static IP via Kickstart Disk RAID1 boot, dedicated NVMe for Ceph DB/WAL RAID1 boot, dedicated NVMe for Ceph DB/WAL

docs.title: 1. Prepare cloud-init image
docs.text:
# Download cloud-init enabled Ubuntu image
wget https://cloud-images.ubuntu.com/noble/current/noble-server-cloudimg-amd64.img
# Or use a local builder (packer) to bake the host baseline into the image

Mirror to internal HTTP server: 

# Internal mirror structure
https://mirror.internal/ubuntu/noble/noble-server-cloudimg-amd64.img

docs.title: 2. User-data template (generated by guide)
docs.text:
The guide generates a user-data.yaml per node with:

#cloud-config
hostname: k8s-cp-1
fqdn: k8s-cp-1.example.com
manage_etc_hosts: true

users:
  - name: ansible
    sudo: ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD:ALL
    ssh_authorized_keys:
      - ssh-ed25519 AAAA... ansible@admin

write_files:
  - path: /etc/network/interfaces.d/50-cloud-init.cfg
    content: |
      auto ens1f0
      iface ens1f0 inet static
        address 10.20.0.11/24
        gateway 10.20.0.1
        dns-nameservers 10.10.0.5 10.10.0.6
  - path: /etc/hosts
    content: |
      127.0.0.1 localhost
      10.20.0.11 k8s-cp-1 k8s-cp-1.example.com
      10.20.0.12 k8s-cp-2 k8s-cp-2.example.com
      10.20.0.13 k8s-cp-3 k8s-cp-3.example.com

runcmd:
  - systemctl disable --now ufw
  - apt-get update && apt-get install -y python3-openstackclient
  - reboot

docs.title: 3. Boot the node
docs.text:
• IPMI virtual media → attach the cloud image
  • Set kernel cmdline: ds=nocloud-net;s=https://user-data.internal/
  • Power on

docs.title: 1. Prepare Kickstart tree
docs.text:
# Mirror the full ISO content
mkdir -p /var/www/html/kickstart/rocky9
mount -o loop Rocky-9.4-x86_64-dvd.iso /mnt
rsync -a /mnt/ /var/www/html/kickstart/rocky9/
umount /mnt

docs.title: 2. Kickstart config (generated by guide)
docs.text:
# /var/www/html/kickstart/rocky9/ks.cfg
install
url --url=http://mirror.internal/kickstart/rocky9
lang en_US.UTF-8
keyboard us
network --bootproto=dhcp --device=link --activate --hostname=k8s-cp-1
rootpw --lock
user --name=ansible --password=$6$salt$hash --iscrypted --groups=wheel
sshkey --username=ansible "ssh-ed25519 AAAA... ansible@admin"
firewall --disabled
selinux --enforcing
timezone --utc Etc/UTC
bootloader --location=mbr --boot-drive=sda
clearpart --all --initlabel --drives=sda
part /boot --fstype=xfs --size=1024 --ondisk=sda
part / --fstype=xfs --size=1 --grow --ondisk=sda
reboot

%packages
@^minimal-environment
python3
openssh-server
sudo
chrony
%end

%post --log=/var/log/anaconda-post.log
# Host baseline from automation/ansible
rpm -ivh http://mirror.internal/packages/ansible-host-baseline-latest.noarch.rpm
systemctl enable --now chronyd
%end

docs.title: 3. PXE boot config
docs.text:
# /var/lib/tftpboot/pxelinux.cfg/default
DEFAULT rocky9
LABEL rocky9
  KERNEL rocky9/vmlinuz
  APPEND initrd=rocky9/initrd.img inst.ks=http://mirror.internal/kickstart/rocky9/ks.cfg ip=dhcp

docs.title: E. After OS install — Ansible host baseline
docs.text:
Both paths converge here. Run the automation playbooks from the admin host:

cd automation/ansible
ansible-playbook -i inventory.ini site.yml \
  -e "target_hosts=k8s-cp-1,k8s-cp-2,k8s-cp-3,k8s-w-1,k8s-w-2" \
  -e "registry_host=harbor.internal" \
  -e "ceph_enabled=true"

This applies: - Kernel tuning (sysctl, transparent hugepages, swappiness) - Container runtime (containerd with registry mirror) - Ceph prerequisites (if using Ceph) - SSH keys, sudo, chrony, firewall baseline

docs.title: F. Generate Kubespray inventory from guide
docs.text:
# From the guide repository
python3 scripts/bundle.py --answers answers/example.json --out dist/
cd dist
./deploy.sh --dry-run    # validates inventory
./deploy.sh              # runs kubespray

The bundle scripts generate hosts.ini and all group_vars from the same answers used for cloud-init/Kickstart user-data — no drift.

docs.title: G. Version matrix
docs.text: This method uses the same Kubespray releases as the standard Kubespray path. See compatibility/version-matrix.md and the "Kubespray → Kubernetes / etcd" matrix on the Deployment page.

docs.title: H. Rollback / re-provision
docs.text:
• cloud-init: Re-deploy user-data, reboot node
  • Kickstart: Reboot node with PXE; Kickstart re-installs cleanly
  • kubespray: Re-run deploy.sh; inventory is idempotent

Source of truth: This document + automation/ansible/ playbooks + compatibility/version-matrix.md + guide bundle scripts.

docs.title: A. Purpose and scope
docs.text:
Document the certificate lifecycle for Kubespray-deployed Kubernetes clusters: certificate types, rotation procedures, OIDC CA provisioning, and expiration handling.

Cross-references kubespray/kubespray-deployment.md §L (OIDC CA certificate provisioning), secrets-management/pki/root-ca-rotation.md, secrets-management/pki/index.md, kubernetes/control-plane/index.md §Certificate lifecycle.

docs.title: B. Certificate types
docs.text: Certificate Issued by Used by Location Rotation kube-apiserver Kubespray PKI kube-apiserver /etc/kubernetes/pki/apiserver.crt Kubespray cluster.yml kubelet Kubespray PKI kubelet /etc/kubernetes/pki/kubelet.crt Kubespray cluster.yml front-proxy-client Kubespray PKI front-proxy /etc/kubernetes/pki/front-proxy-client.crt Kubespray cluster.yml etcd Kubespray PKI etcd /etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/ Kubespray cluster.yml OIDC CA Keycloak TLS issuer kube-apiserver /etc/kubernetes/pki/oidc-ca.crt Manual (owner-operated) service account Kubespray PKI controller-manager /etc/kubernetes/pki/sa.key, sa.crt Kubespray cluster.yml

docs.title: C. Kubespray-managed certificates
docs.text:
Certificates managed by Kubespray are rotated via cluster.yml:

# Rotate all certificates managed by Kubespray
ansible-playbook -i inventory/<cluster>/hosts.ini cluster.yml -b

# Rotate certificates on specific nodes only
ansible-playbook -i inventory/<cluster>/hosts.ini cluster.yml -b --limit <node>

Kubespray regenerates certificates on each run if they're expired or missing. The rotation is automatic — no manual certificate generation is required for Kubespray-managed certs.

docs.title: Rotation procedure
docs.text:
1. Update cluster.yml if certificate parameters changed
  2. Run cluster.yml -b on all control-plane nodes
  3. Verify: kubectl get nodes shows all Ready
  4. Verify: kubectl get --raw='/readyz?verbose' returns all ok

docs.title: D. OIDC CA certificate (manual)
docs.text: The OIDC CA certificate is not managed by Kubespray. It is the CA that signed Keycloak's TLS certificate.

docs.title: Location
docs.text: /etc/kubernetes/pki/oidc-ca.crt on every control-plane node.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
# group_vars/k8s_cluster/k8s-cluster.yml
kube_oidc_ca_file: "/etc/kubernetes/pki/oidc-ca.crt"

docs.title: Rotation procedure (one control-plane node at a time)
docs.text:
1. Replace oidc-ca.crt with the new CA cert on one control-plane node
  2. Restart the kube-apiserver static pod (kubelet recreates it when the manifest changes)
  3. Verify the node is healthy: kubectl get nodes and kubectl get --raw='/readyz?verbose'
  4. Verify OIDC login still works: kubectl auth whoami with a federated user
  5. Repeat for the next control-plane node, one at a time, preserving quorum

Do not restart all control-plane nodes simultaneously — this removes API server quorum and makes the cluster unreachable.

docs.title: Missing certificate behavior
docs.text:
If kube_oidc_ca_file points to a missing file, kube-apiserver fails to start and OIDC authentication is unavailable for the entire cluster. Validate before deploying:

ansible -i inventory/<cluster>/hosts.ini control-plane -m stat -a "path=/etc/kubernetes/pki/oidc-ca.crt"

docs.title: Source certificate
docs.text:
The certificate is the public CA cert (PEM-encoded) that signed keycloak.internal's TLS certificate. It contains no private key and is safe to store in the repository.

Verify it is a CA certificate before deploying:

openssl verify -CAfile oidc-ca.crt oidc-ca.crt
openssl x509 -in oidc-ca.crt -noout -text | grep -A1 'Basic Constraints'

docs.title: Detection
docs.text:
Kubespray does not proactively alert on certificate expiration. Monitor:

# Check kube-apiserver certificate expiry
kubectl -n kube-system get secret <apiserver-cert-secret> -o yaml | \
  grep 'tls.crt:' | head -1 | \
  awk '{print $2}' | base64 -d | openssl x509 -noout -enddate

# Check all certificates
find /etc/kubernetes/pki -name '*.crt' -exec sh -c 'echo "{}:"; openssl x509 -in "{}" -noout -enddate' \;

docs.title: Remediation
docs.text:
• Kubespray-managed certs: Run cluster.yml -b to rotate
  • OIDC CA cert: Follow the manual rotation procedure in Section D
  • etcd certs: Rotated as part of etcd upgrade (lifecycle/upgrades/kubernetes.md)

docs.title: Existing cluster expansion (join / scale)
docs.text: Previous step | Next step

docs.title: A. Purpose and scope
docs.text:
This document describes joining new worker nodes to an already-running Kubernetes cluster. No control-plane reinstall; only worker nodes are added.

Two supported paths:

Path When to use kubeadm join Cluster was bootstrapped with kubeadm; single new nodes or small batches kubespray scale playbook Cluster was deployed with Kubespray; many new nodes, or need idempotent inventory-driven scale

docs.title: Existing cluster must have
docs.text:
• Healthy control plane (all API servers ready, etcd quorum)
  • Reachable Kubernetes API endpoint (VIP or load balancer)
  • kubeadm token or certificate rotation capability for new nodes
  • Same Kubernetes minor version on control plane and new nodes (e.g. both 1.36.x)

docs.title: New nodes must have
docs.text: Item Requirement OS Same OS family and version as existing nodes (Ubuntu 24.04 / OL9 / Rocky 9) Container runtime containerd configured with the same internal registry mirror CNI Cilium (or Calico) binaries and config matching the cluster kubelet Same version pin as control plane (v1.36.x) Network Can reach API server VIP and all pod/service CIDRs Host baseline automation/ansible playbooks applied (kernel, chrony, firewall, etc.)

docs.title: C. Path 1 — kubeadm join (single or few nodes)
1. Generate join token on control plane
docs.text:
# On any control-plane node
kubeadm token create --print-join-command --ttl=24h
# Output example:
# kubeadm join 10.20.0.100:6443 --token abcdef.0123456789abcdef \
#   --discovery-token-ca-cert-hash sha256:abcd...

docs.title: 2. Prepare new node
docs.text:
# On the new node (as root)
# 1. Install same kubelet/kubeadm/kubectl version
yum install -y kubelet-1.36.5 kubeadm-1.36.5 kubectl-1.36.5 --disableexcludes=kubernetes

# 2. Configure containerd with internal registry mirror
cat > /etc/containerd/config.toml <<'EOF'
[plugins."io.containerd.grpc.v1.cri".registry.mirrors."harbor.internal"]
  endpoint = ["https://harbor.internal"]
EOF
systemctl restart containerd

# 3. Install CNI binaries (Cilium)
cilium install --version 1.20.3

# 4. Run join command from step 1
kubeadm join 10.20.0.100:6443 --token abcdef.0123456789abcdef \
  --discovery-token-ca-cert-hash sha256:abcd...

docs.title: 3. Verify
docs.text:
kubectl get nodes -o wide
kubectl wait --for=condition=Ready node/<new-node-name> --timeout=5m

docs.title: D. Path 2 — Kubespray scale playbook (many nodes, idempotent)
1. Update inventory
docs.text:
Add new worker nodes to kubespray/inventory/<cluster>/hosts.ini:

[control-plane]
k8s-cp-1 ansible_host=10.20.0.11 ip=10.20.0.11
k8s-cp-2 ansible_host=10.20.0.12 ip=10.20.0.12
k8s-cp-3 ansible_host=10.20.0.13 ip=10.20.0.13

[etcd]
k8s-cp-1
k8s-cp-2
k8s-cp-3

[kube-node]
k8s-w-1 ansible_host=10.20.0.21 ip=10.20.0.21
k8s-w-2 ansible_host=10.20.0.22 ip=10.20.0.22
# NEW NODES BELOW
k8s-w-3 ansible_host=10.20.0.23 ip=10.20.0.23
k8s-w-4 ansible_host=10.20.0.24 ip=10.20.0.24

docs.title: 2. Run scale playbook
docs.text:
cd kubespray
# Use the same virtualenv as the original deploy
source .venv/bin/activate

# Limit to new nodes only (scale playbook is idempotent on existing)
ansible-playbook -i inventory/<cluster>/hosts.ini scale.yml \
  --limit "k8s-w-3,k8s-w-4" \
  -e "ansible_user=ansible"

The scale.yml playbook: - Runs host baseline on new nodes only - Joins them to the existing cluster - Does not touch control plane or existing workers

docs.title: 3. Verify
docs.text:
kubectl get nodes -o wide
# New nodes should show Ready

docs.title: E. Version matrix
docs.text:
This method uses the same Kubespray releases as the standard Kubespray path. The kubesprayRelease value in the guide answers must match the release that built the existing cluster. See compatibility/version-matrix.md and the "Kubespray → Kubernetes / etcd" matrix on the Deployment page.

Constraint Rule Kubernetes minor New nodes must match control plane minor (1.36.x → 1.36.x) Kubespray release Must match the release used for the original deploy containerd Same version as cluster (pinned by Kubespray release) CNI Same CNI and version as cluster

docs.title: F. Adding specialized node types
docs.text: Node type Additional steps GPU workers Install NVIDIA driver + GPU Operator on new nodes before join; label nvidia.com/gpu.present=true Edge workers Add to edge group in inventory; MetalLB/keepalived config may need update Ceph OSD Not via this path — use cephadm or Rook to add OSDs to storage cluster separately

docs.title: G. Replacing a failed worker
docs.text:
1. Cordon & drain the failed node: kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data
  2. Delete node: kubectl delete node <node>
  3. Re-provision replacement with same IP/hostname (or new IP, update inventory)
  4. Join via kubeadm or kubespray scale as above

docs.title: H. Rollback
docs.text:
• kubeadm join: kubeadm reset on the new node, then re-join
  • kubespray scale: Re-run scale playbook; it's idempotent

Source of truth: This document + kubespray/scale.yml + compatibility/version-matrix.md + guide bundle scripts.

docs.title: Core group vars — reference template
docs.text: Copy to kubespray/inventory/<cluster>/group_vars/. Every value must be verified against the pinned Kubespray release before use; the variable names change between releases.

docs.title: group_vars/k8s_cluster/k8s-cluster.yml
docs.text:
# Kubernetes version. Must be inside the pinned Kubespray release's supported
# range (floor v1.34.0 for release-2.32).
kube_version: v1.36.5

# CNI. The release ships cilium 1.20.3.
kube_network_plugin: cilium

# Disable kube-proxy; Cilium replaces it. Requires k8sServiceHost/Port below.
kube_proxy_mode: ""

# Pod and service CIDRs. One pair per cluster.
kube_pods_subnet: "10.30.0.0/16"
kube_service_addresses: "10.32.0.0/16"

# Cilium needs the API endpoint when kube-proxy is absent.
k8sServiceHost: "10.20.0.100"      # the control-plane VIP
k8sServicePort: 6443

enable_coredns: true

docs.title: group_vars/all/main.yml
docs.text:
container_manager: containerd
containerd_version: "2.3.7"        # the version release-2.32 ships

# Cert-manager and Argo CD are installed by Argo CD, not by Kubespray.
cert_manager: false

# Node labels applied by Kubespray, if any.
kube_node_labels: {}

docs.title: group_vars/all/offline.yml
docs.text:
# Internal registry and file mirror. See the Kubespray release-2.32 offline guide.
kube_image_repo: "{{ registry_host }}"
gcr_image_repo: "{{ registry_host }}"
docker_image_repo: "{{ registry_host }}"
quay_image_repo: "{{ registry_host }}"
github_image_repo: "{{ registry_host }}"

github_url: "{{ files_repo }}/github.com"
dl_k8s_io_url: "{{ files_repo }}/dl.k8s.io"
storage_googleapis_url: "{{ files_repo }}/storage.googleapis.com"
get_helm_url: "{{ files_repo }}/get.helm.sh"

local_path_provisioner_helper_image_repo: "{{ registry_host }}/busybox"

# containerd 2+ mirrors
containerd_registries_mirrors:
  - prefix: docker.io
    mirrors:
      - host: https://registry-1.docker.io
        capabilities: ["pull", "resolve"]
        skip_verify: false
  - prefix: "{{ registry_addr }}"
    mirrors:
      - host: "https://{{ registry_addr }}"
        capabilities: ["pull", "resolve"]
        skip_verify: false
        header:
          Authorization: "Basic {{ (registry_user + ':' + registry_pass) | b64encode }}"

# Cilium chart served from the internal file mirror
cilium_install_extra_flags: "--repository {{ files_repo }}/helm.cilium.io/"
cilium_extra_values:
  image:
    useDigest: false
  hubble:
    relay:
      image:
        useDigest: false
    ui:
      backend:
        image:
          useDigest: false
      frontend:
        image:
          useDigest: false
  operator:
    image:
      override: "{{ registry_host }}/cilium/operator-generic:v1.20.3"
      useDigest: false
      extension: ""
  certgen:
    image:
      useDigest: false
  envoy:
    image:
      useDigest: false

# OS package repositories (Oracle Linux / RHEL family)
containerd_rh_repo_base_url: "{{ yum_repo }}/containerd"
containerd_rh_repo_gpgkey: "{{ yum_repo }}/containerd/gpg"

# OS package repositories (Ubuntu)
containerd_ubuntu_repo_base_url: "{{ ubuntu_repo }}/containerd"
containerd_ubuntu_repo_gpgkey: "{{ ubuntu_repo }}/containerd/gpg"
containerd_ubuntu_repo_repokey: 'YOURREPOKEY'

docs.title: site variables (not in this file)
docs.text: registry_host, registry_addr, registry_user, registry_pass, files_repo, yum_repo, ubuntu_repo come from the environment overlay (site-<env>) or from Ansible Vault. They are never committed.

docs.title: Verify before use
docs.text:
# Confirm the variable names exist in the pinned release
grep -rn "kube_proxy_mode\|k8sServiceHost" roles/kubespray_defaults/defaults/main/ | head
grep -rn "containerd_registries_mirrors" roles/ | head

docs.title: 📋 Purpose and Scope
docs.text:
Document Kubespray inventory design: Ansible inventory structure, group variable organization, host variables, inventory templates, variable precedence, and validation procedures for production deployments.

Cross-references kubespray/kubespray-deployment.md §Inventory, kubespray/group-vars-template.md, kubespray/inventory-architecture.md.

docs.title: 📁 Inventory Directory Structure
docs.text:
kubespray/
├── VERSION                      # pinned Kubespray release tag
├── inventory/
│   ├── sample/                  # vendored copy of the release's sample inventory
│   └── <cluster>/
│       ├── hosts.ini            # host definitions and groups
│       └── group_vars/
│           ├── all/
│           │   ├── main.yml     # all-host variables
│           │   ├── offline.yml  # image + registry overrides
│           │   └── containerd.yml  # registry mirror + TLS config
│           ├── k8s_cluster/
│           │   ├── k8s-cluster.yml     # version, CNI, networking
│           │   └── k8s-cluster-encrypted-images.yml
│           ├── etcd/
│           ├── kube_node/
│           └── k8s_secrets/
│       └── group_vars/all/external.yml
└── patches/                     # site-specific variable overrides

docs.title: Core Layout
docs.text:
[all:vars]
ansible_user=ansible
ansible_become=yes
ansible_python_interpreter=/usr/bin/python3
ansible_ssh_common_args='-o StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new'

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Control plane (3 nodes, stacked etcd)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
[control-plane]
k8s-cp-1 ansible_host=10.20.0.11 ip=10.20.0.11
k8s-cp-2 ansible_host=10.20.0.12 ip=10.20.0.12
k8s-cp-3 ansible_host=10.20.0.13 ip=10.20.0.13

[etcd]
k8s-cp-1
k8s-cp-2
k8s-cp-3

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Workers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
[k8s-node]
k8s-w-1 ansible_host=10.20.0.21 ip=10.20.0.21
k8s-w-2 ansible_host=10.20.0.22 ip=10.20.0.22
k8s-w-3 ansible_host=10.20.0.23 ip=10.20.0.23

# GPU pool: a separate group so labels and taints can differ
[k8s-node:children]
gpu-node

[gpu-node]
k8s-gpu-1 ansible_host=10.50.0.11 ip=10.50.0.11 labels='{"accelerator":"nvidia"}'

# Storage pool: dedicated OSD hosts
[k8s-node:children]
storage-node

[storage-node]
k8s-st-1 ansible_host=10.40.0.11 ip=10.40.0.11
k8s-st-2 ansible_host=10.40.0.12 ip=10.40.0.12
k8s-st-3 ansible_host=10.40.0.13 ip=10.40.0.13

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Groups Kubespray expects
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
[kube-master]
control-plane

[kube-node]
control-plane
k8s-node

[calico-node]

[k8s-cluster:children]
control-plane
etcd
k8s-node

docs.title: Rules
docs.text: Rule Description etcd members Must also be in control-plane when etcd is stacked k8s-node Must contain every worker, including GPU pool No double-listing Never list a host in two k8s-node groups ip= Must be the address on the cluster network, not the management address

docs.title: File Purpose
docs.text: File Purpose group_vars/all/main.yml Container manager, runtime, subnets, cert-manager group_vars/all/offline.yml Image repo overrides, registry mirrors, files_repo group_vars/all/containerd.yml Registry mirror, TLS config group_vars/k8s_cluster/k8s-cluster.yml kube_version, CNI, proxy mode, subnets group_vars/k8s_cluster/k8s-cluster-encrypted-images.yml Encrypted image variables group_vars/etcd/ etcd version, storage backend group_vars/kube_node/ kubelet config, node labels group_vars/k8s_secrets/ Encrypted secrets (Vault references)

docs.title: Verification Before Use
docs.text:
1. Confirm variable names exist in the pinned Kubespray release:
# Example verification
grep -rn "kube_proxy_mode\|k8sServiceHost" roles/kubespray_defaults/defaults/main/ | head
grep -rn "containerd_registries_mirrors" roles/ | head

  1. Never reuse a group-vars file across a Kubespray release without diffing it against the new release's inventory/sample.

  2. Variables registry_host, registry_addr, registry_user, registry_pass, files_repo, yum_repo, ubuntu_repo come from the environment overlay (site-<env>) or from Ansible Vault. They are never committed to Git.

docs.title: Per-Host Variables Placement
docs.text: Host-specific variables go into host_vars/<hostname>.yml files, or can be placed inline in hosts.ini using the variable=value syntax after the hostname.

docs.title: Example host_vars file
docs.text:
# host_vars/k8s-cp-1.yml
ansible_user: ansible
ansible_become: yes
kube_api_server_ip: 10.20.0.11
kube_api_server_port: 6443

docs.title: Inline in hosts.ini
docs.text: k8s-cp-1 ansible_host=10.20.0.11 ip=10.20.0.11 ansible_ssh_private_key_file=~/.ssh/id_rsa

docs.title: Variable Precedence (Ansible)
docs.text:
Ansible resolves variables in this order (lowest to highest priority):

  1. Default variables — in library/ or module defaults
  2. Group vars — group_vars/all/ and group_vars/<group>/
  3. Host vars — host_vars/<hostname>.yml and inline in inventory
  4. Play vars — vars assigned in a play
  5. Play var priority — set_fact, set_hierarchy, etc.
  6. Extra vars — -e flag or vars_prompt

Production guideline: Place production-specific overrides in patches/ directory, never directly in group_vars/ that are committed from the base Kubespray release.

docs.title: Complete Precedence Chain
docs.text:
1.     DEFAULT                                 # module defaults
2.     VARIABLES                               # command-line / -e
3.     PLAY-VARS                               # vars: set_fact, etc.
4.     ROLE-VARS                               # defaults/
5.     INVENTORY-VARS                          # group_vars/ host_vars/
6.     PLAY-VARS-PRIORITY                       # priority: set_fact
7.     FACTS                                    # gathered by setup
8.     ROLEx-DEFAULT                          # role defaults
9.     ROLEx-VARS                             # role vars/
10. SITE-DEFINED VARIABLES                   # site.yml, etc.

docs.title: Production Deployment Guidelines
docs.text:
Situation Recommended Location Cluster-wide defaults (CNI, version) group_vars/k8s_cluster/k8s-cluster.yml All hosts (container manager, subnets) group_vars/all/main.yml Per-node overrides (labels, taints) group_vars/kube_node/ or host_vars/ Secrets (certs, keys) group_vars/k8s_secrets/ with Vault references Site-specific overrides (registry, storage) patches/site-<env>.yml Release-specific adjustments Diff against inventory/sample/

Never commit variables that change between Kubespray releases without verifying compatibility.

docs.title: 1. Syntax Check
docs.text:
# From the repo root
ansible -i kubespray/inventory/<cluster>/hosts.ini all -m ping
ansible-playbook -i kubespray/inventory/<cluster>/hosts.ini cluster.yml --syntax-check

docs.title: 2. Inventory Link Validation
docs.text:
Run the repository's link checker:

python3 scripts/check_links.py

This validates: - Relative markdown file references - In-page anchors point to existing headings - No broken links in documentation

docs.title: 3. Cluster Compatibility Verification
docs.text:
# Check pinned Kubespray release matches group vars
grep "kube_version:" kubespray/inventory/<cluster>/group_vars/all/main.yml

# Verify variable names against release
grep -rn "kube_proxy_mode\|k8sServiceHost" roles/kubespray_defaults/defaults/main/ | head

docs.title: 4. Production Checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] All hosts have ansible_host and ip set to cluster-network addresses
  • [ ] etcd members are also in control-plane (when stacked)
  • [ ] Every worker (including GPU/storage) is in k8s-node group
  • [ ] No host appears in two k8s-node groups
  • [ ] ip= uses cluster network address, not management address
  • [ ] Group vars verified against pinned Kubespray release
  • [ ] No uncommitted Vault secrets or registry credentials
  • [ ] Syntax check passes without errors
  • [ ] check_links.py reports 0 broken links

docs.title: A. Purpose and scope

docs.title: E. Group vars — core
docs.text:
group_vars/k8s_cluster/k8s-cluster.yml (names must be verified against the pinned release's sample):

kube_version: v1.31.x            # VERIFY per release
kube_network_plugin: cilium
kube_proxy_mode: ""
enable_coredns: true
kube_pods_subnet: "10.30.0.0/16"
kube_service_addresses: "10.32.0.0/16"

kube_proxy_mode: "" disables kube-proxy. This is required for Cilium's kube-proxy-free mode. It is a per-release variable name — verify before use.

group_vars/all/main.yml:

container_manager: containerd
containerd_version: "1.7.x"      # VERIFY per release
containerd_enable_cri: true
kube_pods_subnet: "10.30.0.0/16"
kube_service_addresses: "10.32.0.0/16"
cert_manager: false              # installed by Argo CD, not Kubespray

docs.title: F. Offline image configuration
docs.text:
Kubespray downloads images from the upstream registry. In an air-gapped environment, mirror every required image and point Kubespray at the internal registry.

Verified against the Kubespray release-2.32 official offline guide (docs/operations/offline-environment.md), check date 2026-10-17.

The upstream guide requires four internal services:

  1. An HTTP reverse proxy / cache / mirror serving static files (binaries, zips) — the files_repo.
  2. An internal Yum/Deb repository for OS packages.
  3. An internal container image registry populated with every image Kubespray uses.
  4. Optional internal PyPI and Helm registries.

The upstream tip for files_repo is to preserve the original domain as the top-level directory (github.com/, dl.k8s.io/, storage.googleapis.com/, get.helm.sh/). Do that — it makes the mapping mechanical and reviewable.

docs.title: Inventory variables (official names)
docs.text:
# group_vars/all/offline.yml
# Registry overrides
kube_image_repo: "{{ registry_host }}"
gcr_image_repo: "{{ registry_host }}"
docker_image_repo: "{{ registry_host }}"
quay_image_repo: "{{ registry_host }}"
github_image_repo: "{{ registry_host }}"
github_url: "{{ files_repo }}/github.com"
dl_k8s_io_url: "{{ files_repo }}/dl.k8s.io"
storage_googleapis_url: "{{ files_repo }}/storage.googleapis.com"
get_helm_url: "{{ files_repo }}/get.helm.sh"
local_path_provisioner_helper_image_repo: "{{ registry_host }}/busybox"

# containerd 2+ registry mirrors
containerd_registries_mirrors:
  - prefix: docker.io
    mirrors:
      - host: https://registry-1.docker.io
        capabilities: ["pull", "resolve"]
        skip_verify: false
  - prefix: "{{ registry_addr }}"
    mirrors:
      - host: "https://{{ registry_addr }}"
        capabilities: ["pull", "resolve"]
        skip_verify: false
        header:
          Authorization: "Basic {{ (registry_user + ':' + registry_pass) | b64encode }}"

# Cilium: mirror the chart index and the chart tarball into files_repo
cilium_install_extra_flags: "--repository {{ files_repo }}/helm.cilium.io/"
cilium_extra_values:
  image:
    useDigest: false
  hubble:
    relay:
      image:
        useDigest: false
    ui:
      backend:
        image:
          useDigest: false
      frontend:
        image:
          useDigest: false
  operator:
    image:
      override: "{{ registry_host }}/cilium/operator-generic:v<VERSION>"
      useDigest: false
      extension: ""
  certgen:
    image:
      useDigest: false
  envoy:
    image:
      useDigest: false

Required variable definitions, from the upstream guide:

Variable Meaning registry_host Container image registry. If the internal registry uses the same repository paths as upstream, no per-image overrides are needed registry_addr Registry as [domain or ip]:[port] only files_repo HTTP server or reverse proxy serving the static file tree. Include the version in the path so an upgrade does not change the URL yum_repo / debian_repo / ubuntu_repo Internal OS package repository for the matching OS registry_user / registry_pass Registry credentials, stored with !vault

Keeping the same repository paths in the internal registry is the single biggest simplification: it means the *_image_repo overrides above are the only change and the image list does not have to be rewritten.

docs.title: containerd registry auth — version matters
docs.text:
Kubespray release-2.32 documents two different mechanisms, because containerd changed its registry configuration:

# containerd 2+ -> hosts.toml style mirrors
containerd_registries_mirrors:
  - prefix: "{{ registry_addr }}"
    mirrors:
      - host: "https://{{ registry_addr }}"
        capabilities: ["pull", "resolve"]
        header:
          Authorization: "Basic {{ (registry_user + ':' + registry_pass) | b64encode }}"

# containerd 1.7 -> legacy auth list
containerd_registry_auth:
  - registry: "{{ registry_host }}"
    username: "{{ registry_user }}"
    password: "{{ registry_pass }}"

This platform pins containerd 2.3.7 (the version Kubespray release-2.32 ships), so the containerd_registries_mirrors form is the correct one.

docs.title: Generating the artifact list
docs.text:
The upstream guide provides contrib/offline/generate_list.sh, which reads roles/kubespray_defaults/defaults/main/download.yml and produces the file and image list templates, then expands them with Ansible.

# In a connected environment, with the pinned Kubespray checkout
cd contrib/offline
./generate_list.sh

It emits: - temp/files.list.template — the static files (binaries, zips) to mirror. - temp/images.list.template — every container image, with the kube-apiserver, kube-controller-manager, kube-scheduler, and kube-proxy images added separately because kubeadm pulls those and they are not in download.yml.

The same guide also offers a Kubespray container image (quay.io/kubespray/kubespray) with all Python dependencies baked in — mirror that image and run the playbooks inside it. It removes the Python dependency-closure problem from the offline environment entirely.

docs.title: OS package repositories
docs.text:
# Oracle Linux / RHEL family
containerd_rh_repo_base_url: "{{ yum_repo }}/containerd"
containerd_rh_repo_gpgkey: "{{ yum_repo }}/containerd/gpg"

# Ubuntu
containerd_ubuntu_repo_base_url: "{{ ubuntu_repo }}/containerd"
containerd_ubuntu_repo_gpgkey: "{{ ubuntu_repo }}/containerd/gpg"
containerd_ubuntu_repo_repokey: 'YOURREPOKEY'

The upstream guide notes that only the container runtime packages come from these repositories; other packages come from the base OS repositories, which must also be mirrored.

docs.title: Alternative and less preferred
docs.text: A Kubespray image-repository override that rewrites every image path to a differently-named internal path also works, but it requires the exact variable names in the pinned release and a rewritten image list. Use it only when the internal registry cannot mirror the upstream repository paths.

docs.title: G. Deployment
docs.text:
Execution context: Automation Management Server (or a bastion with the Ansible venv).

# 1. Pre-check
ansible -i inventory/<cluster>/hosts.ini all -m ping
ansible-playbook -i inventory/<cluster>/hosts.ini cluster.yml --syntax-check
ansible-playbook -i inventory/<cluster>/hosts.ini cluster.yml -b --check --diff --limit control-plane

# 2. Deploy
ansible-playbook -i inventory/<cluster>/hosts.ini cluster.yml -b

# 3. Post-check
kubectl get nodes -o wide
kubectl get pods -A

docs.title: H. Idempotency and reruns
docs.text:
Kubespray is idempotent by design. Reruns are safe and are the normal way to apply a corrected variable. A rerun after a failed deploy is the recommended recovery step, not a fresh install.

Rules: - Never delete /etc/kubernetes to "start clean" on a node that holds state. Use kubespray reset (see below) as the intended teardown. - Keep the inventory and group vars in Git so a rerun is reproducible from the recorded state.

docs.title: I. Node lifecycle
docs.text: Task Procedure Add worker Add to k8s-node in hosts.ini, run cluster.yml --limit <host> Add control-plane Add to control-plane and etcd, run cluster.yml --limit <host> Remove worker kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data, remove from inventory, cluster.yml --limit <host> Replace worker Drain + remove + rebuild the host via Ansible + re-add Remove control-plane Requires care: etcd membership must be removed first, then the host Reset a node ansible-playbook ... reset.yml --limit <host> (Kubespray-provided), then rebuild

docs.title: J. Upgrades
docs.text:
Upgrades are managed by Kubespray: set the new kube_version in group vars and re-run cluster.yml. The upgrade is sequential (one node at a time) and control-plane nodes are upgraded first.

Constraints: - Kubernetes supports only one minor version skew in each direction. Do not skip minors. - The kubeadm version must be compatible with the target Kubernetes version. - etcd is upgraded as part of the node upgrade. - CNI and CSI may need separate upgrades. Plan them explicitly. - Rollback of a Kubernetes minor version is not supported. Take a snapshot before starting.

Full procedure with the upgrade-order checklist: lifecycle/upgrades/kubernetes.md.

docs.title: K. Validation
docs.text:
kubectl get nodes -o wide
kubectl get --raw='/readyz?verbose'
kubectl -n kube-system get pods
etcdctl --endpoints=https://127.0.0.1:2379 endpoint health --cluster \
  --cacert=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/ca.crt \
  --cert=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/healthcheck-client.crt \
  --key=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/healthcheck-client.key

docs.title: L. OIDC CA certificate provisioning
docs.text: The kube-apiserver OIDC integration requires a CA certificate at kube_oidc_ca_file (/etc/kubernetes/pki/oidc-ca.crt by default) on every control-plane node. This cert is the CA that signed Keycloak's TLS certificate, not an arbitrary server certificate.

docs.title: Status: documented requirement, not implemented
docs.text:
CA certificate provisioning is a deployment requirement, not an implemented repository playbook. The example Ansible copy task below is illustrative only — it is not present anywhere in the repository, and no files/oidc-ca.crt is committed. The environment owner must supply the verified CA certificate and install it on every control-plane node before kube-apiserver starts with OIDC enabled.

An ingress TLS secret must not be assumed to contain the issuing CA certificate. The CA cert must be obtained directly from the Keycloak TLS certificate issuer (internal CA or cert-manager-issued cert).

docs.title: Source certificate input
docs.text:
The certificate is the public CA cert (PEM-encoded) that signed keycloak.internal's TLS certificate. It contains no private key and is safe to store in the repository.

Verify it is a CA certificate (not a leaf/server cert) before deploying:

openssl verify -CAfile oidc-ca.crt oidc-ca.crt
openssl x509 -in oidc-ca.crt -noout -text | grep -A1 'Basic Constraints'

docs.title: Distribution mechanism (owner-supplied)
docs.text:
The environment owner provisions the cert using Ansible or their preferred configuration management. Example (illustrative, not implemented in this repo):

# group_vars/k8s_cluster/k8s-cluster.yml (addition)
kube_oidc_ca_file: "/etc/kubernetes/pki/oidc-ca.crt"

# Ansible copy task (site playbook, not in this repo)
- name: Provision OIDC CA certificate
  copy:
    src: files/oidc-ca.crt
    dest: "{{ kube_oidc_ca_file }}"
    owner: root
    group: root
    mode: "0644"
  delegate_to: "{{ inventory_hostname }}"
  run_once: false

docs.title: Idempotency
docs.text: Ansible copy is idempotent: reruns are safe and do not rewrite an unchanged file.

docs.title: Rotation procedure
docs.text:
kube-apiserver reads kube_oidc_ca_file as a static file at startup. When the CA file changes, kube-apiserver does not auto-reload it; the static pod/container must be restarted. Kubespray deploys kube-apiserver as a kubeadm static pod managed by the kubelet.

The exact restart mechanism depends on the host's kubelet configuration and is not universally standardized across distributions. Do not assume systemctl restart kube-apiserver exists — kube-apiserver is typically not a systemd service when deployed via Kubespray/kubeadm static pods.

One-control-plane-at-a-time procedure (verify before production use):

  1. On one control-plane node, replace oidc-ca.crt with the new CA cert.
  2. Restart the kube-apiserver static pod (kubelet recreates it when its manifest changes, or delete the static pod manifest and let kubelet re-instantiate).
  3. Verify the node is healthy: kubectl get nodes and kubectl get --raw='/readyz?verbose'.
  4. Verify OIDC login still works: kubectl auth whoami with a federated user.
  5. Repeat for the next control-plane node, one at a time, preserving quorum.

Do not restart all control-plane nodes simultaneously — this would remove API server quorum and make the cluster unreachable.

docs.title: Missing certificate behavior
docs.text:
If kube_oidc_ca_file points to a missing file, kube-apiserver fails to start and OIDC authentication is unavailable for the entire cluster. Validate the file exists before deploying:

ansible -i inventory/<cluster>/hosts.ini control-plane -m stat -a "path=/etc/kubernetes/pki/oidc-ca.crt"

docs.title: Repository does not automate CA rotation
docs.text: No certificate renewal, rotation scheduler, or automated restart mechanism is implemented in this repository. Rotation is a manual, owner-operated procedure.

docs.title: M. Best practices
docs.text:
Mandatory: - Pin the Kubespray release in kubespray/VERSION; never track master. - Keep the inventory and group vars in Git; the cluster must be reproducible from the repo. - Mirror every image the deploy uses, verified by a pull test in the offline environment. - Keep kubespray reset available as the documented node teardown path. - Run --check --diff on the control-plane before any real run.

Strongly recommended: - Keep a patches/ directory for site-specific overrides so they are visible in review. - Run the deploy from the Automation Management Server, never from a laptop that also runs a browser. - Record the Ansible and Python versions in requirements.txt and pin them.

Previous step | Next step

docs.title: Kubespray multi-version support
docs.text: Check date: 2026-10-17. All values extracted from each release branch's own README and docs/ansible/ansible.md by scripts/kubespray_release_matrix.py and scripts/kubespray_ansible_matrix.py.

docs.title: Why five versions
docs.text:
A Kubespray release pins the exact Kubernetes, etcd, containerd, CNI, and Helm versions it was tested with. A single pinned release means a single point of failure: when that release ages out, or when a site needs a Kubernetes version that release cannot deploy, the whole estate is blocked on one upgrade.

The platform therefore supports five Kubespray release branches at once: release-2.28 through release-2.32. Each is a complete, deployable, offline-capable configuration.

docs.title: The support matrix
docs.text:
Kubespray release Kubernetes (default) Min Kubernetes etcd containerd Helm Cilium Calico Ansible Python release-2.32 1.36.5 v1.34.0 3.6.15 2.3.7 3.22.0 1.20.3 3.31.7 >= 2.19.0, < 2.20.0 3.11 - 3.13 release-2.31 1.35.9 v1.30 3.6.15 2.2.10 3.18.4 1.19.3 3.31.7 >= 2.18.0, < 2.19.0 3.11 - 3.13 release-2.30 1.34.12 v1.30 3.5.34 2.2.10 3.18.4 1.18.6 3.30.7 >= 2.17.3 3.10 - 3.12 release-2.29 1.33.10 v1.30 3.5.29 2.1.6 3.18.4 1.18.5 3.30.7 >= 2.17.3 3.10 - 3.12 release-2.28 1.32.13 v1.30 3.5.29 2.0.7 3.16.4 1.17.9 3.29.7 >= 2.16.4 3.10 - 3.12

Each row is a full configuration, not just a Kubernetes version. The etcd, containerd, Helm, and CNI versions in a row are the ones that release ships and tests. Do not mix a containerd from one row into an inventory from another.

docs.title: Deployment model: one checkout per release
docs.text:
kubespray/
├── VERSION                        # the default release for new clusters
├── releases/
│   ├── release-2.28/              # a full git clone at that tag
│   ├── release-2.29/
│   ├── release-2.30/
│   ├── release-2.31/
│   └── release-2.32/
├── inventory/
│   ├── prod/                      # uses release-2.32
│   ├── prod-legacy/               # uses release-2.29
│   └── staging/
└── virtualenvs/
    ├── release-2.28-venv/         # ansible 2.16.x, python 3.11
    ├── ...
    └── release-2.32-venv/         # ansible 2.19.x, python 3.12

Rule: one virtualenv per Kubespray release. The Ansible version differs between releases (2.16.4 to 2.19.0), and a shared virtualenv will break one of them. Each venv installs that release's own requirements.txt.

# Per-release environment
for r in 2.28 2.29 2.30 2.31 2.32; do
  python3 -m venv /opt/kubespray/venvs/release-$r
  /opt/kubespray/venvs/release-$r/bin/pip install -r /opt/kubespray/releases/release-$r/requirements.txt
done

Each venv also needs the platform's own collection and role versions, installed from the internal Nexus.

docs.title: Inventory model: one inventory per (cluster, release) pair
docs.text:
A cluster is bound to the Kubespray release that built it. The binding is recorded in the inventory directory name and in a kubespray-release marker in the cluster's group vars.

inventory/
├── prod/                    # release-2.32
│   ├── hosts.ini
│   └── group_vars/
├── prod-legacy/             # release-2.29, pinned until the site migrates
│   ├── hosts.ini
│   └── group_vars/
│       └── all/
│           └── kubespray-release.yml
└── staging/                 # release-2.32

# group_vars/all/kubespray-release.yml
kubespray_release: release-2.29
kubernetes_target: v1.33.10

Why one inventory per pair rather than one inventory with a variable:

  • The group-vars differ between releases (variable names change). A single inventory would accumulate conditional variables for five releases, and every run would carry dead configuration.
  • A rerun must reproduce the cluster exactly as it was built. The inventory is that record.
  • Upgrading a cluster to a newer Kubespray release is a separate operation with its own change record.

docs.title: Offline artifacts: one set per release
docs.text:
Each release needs its own image set and file tree, because the component versions differ.

files_repo/
├── release-2.28/
│   ├── github.com/
│   ├── dl.k8s.io/
│   ├── storage.googleapis.com/
│   ├── get.helm.sh/
│   └── helm.cilium.io/
├── release-2.29/
...

The files_repo URL carries the release in the path, exactly as the Kubespray offline guide recommends, so an upgrade does not change the base URL.

Image sets are per release and per containerd version. The kube-apiserver, kube-controller-manager, kube-scheduler, and kube-proxy images differ per Kubernetes version, and the CNI, etcd, and pause images differ per release. The Kubespray contrib/offline/generate_list.sh script produces the list per release; run it in each release's checkout.

Harbor layout that keeps the versions distinguishable:

harbor.internal/
├── kubespray/release-2.28/     # mirrors upstream repository paths
├── kubespray/release-2.29/
├── kubespray/release-2.30/
├── kubespray/release-2.31/
├── kubespray/release-2.32/
└── platform/                    # everything that is not Kubespray-managed

Because each release's images are mirrored under the same upstream repository path inside a per-release project, the inventory for that release points at its own project with no per-image overrides.

docs.title: Lifecycle of a supported release
docs.text:
Stage Meaning Duration Action Supported Fully deployable, upgrades in, security fixes tracked Current + 4 predecessors New clusters may use it. Upgrades in are allowed from the next-newer release only Maintenance Deployable for new clusters, but no new clusters should adopt it Until the successor's successor ships Freeze the inventory. Continue mirroring artifacts. Plan the migration Deprecated Deployable for rebuilds only. Not for new clusters and not for upgrades 3 months after entering Maintenance Artifact mirror retained. New installs blocked by policy Retired Removed from the platform At the end of Deprecation Artifacts and the checkout archived offline

Rules:

  • A release leaves "Supported" only when a fifth successor exists. That is what keeps five versions supported.
  • A release stays in "Supported" for at least 12 months after its successor ships, unless a critical CVE in the pinned Kubernetes version forces an earlier exit. A CVE forces an emergency exit, and that exit is recorded with the CVE.
  • A Kubernetes version that reaches end of life removes that combination from the matrix immediately. The Kubespray release stays, but the Kubernetes version is no longer deployable.

docs.title: Kubernetes version coverage across the five releases
docs.text:
release-2.28  ->  Kubernetes 1.32.x
release-2.29  ->  Kubernetes 1.33.x
release-2.30  ->  Kubernetes 1.34.x
release-2.31  ->  Kubernetes 1.35.x
release-2.32  ->  Kubernetes 1.36.x  (floor v1.34.0)

Together they cover five consecutive Kubernetes minor versions. A cluster that must stay on an older Kubernetes minor (a vendor support constraint, a workload that has not been certified on a newer version) is still deployable, and the platform can rebuild it.

docs.title: Upgrade ladder
docs.text:
Kubernetes supports one minor of skew in each direction, so a cluster moves one minor at a time. The ladder across the supported releases:

release-2.28 (1.32)  ->  release-2.29 (1.33)  ->  release-2.30 (1.34)
     ->  release-2.31 (1.35)  ->  release-2.32 (1.36)

Procedure for one step:

  1. Create a new inventory directory for the target release, copying the hosts and the site-specific group vars.
  2. Set kubespray_release and kubernetes_target in the new inventory.
  3. Mirror the target release's artifacts and pull-verify them.
  4. Run the target release's cluster.yml against the new inventory, with the target release's venv.
  5. Validate: kubectl get nodes, kubectl get pods -A, the CSI and CNI versions, and the application smoke tests.
  6. Keep the old inventory and the old release checkout until the validation window closes.

The Ansible version changes between some steps (2.17.3 -> 2.18.0 -> 2.19.0). The venv is per release, so each step uses its own.

docs.title: Validation of the support matrix
docs.text:
# The extracted matrix, refreshed from upstream
python3 scripts/kubespray_release_matrix.py release-2.28 release-2.29 release-2.30 release-2.31 release-2.32
python3 scripts/kubespray_ansible_matrix.py release-2.28 release-2.29 release-2.30 release-2.31 release-2.32

# The offline artifacts for a release are present
for r in 2.28 2.29 2.30 2.31 2.32; do
  test -d "files_repo/release-$r" || echo "MISSING files_repo for release-$r"
done

docs.title: Best practices
docs.text:
Mandatory: - One checkout, one virtualenv, and one inventory per Kubespray release. - The Kubernetes, etcd, containerd, CNI, and Helm versions in an inventory are the ones that release ships. Do not mix. - The release in use is recorded in the inventory and in the cluster's own labels. - Artifacts for every supported release are mirrored and pull-verified, not just the current one. - A cluster moves one Kubernetes minor at a time.

Strongly recommended: - The deprecated-stage release list is reviewed at every platform release meeting, and the resulting decision is recorded as an ADR amendment. - A rebuild drill against the oldest supported release, at least annually, to prove the estate can be rebuilt on a pinned older combination. - The per-release files_repo trees are stored on the offline media as well as the internal mirror.

docs.title: Offline Deployment Test Procedure
docs.text: Previous step | Next step

docs.title: A. Purpose and scope
docs.text:
Offline deployment test = Verified end-to-end procedure for deploying Kubespray/Kubernetes in an air-gapped environment with no external egress. This procedure validates that all required artifacts (container images, OS packages, Helm charts, binaries) are properly mirrored and that the bootstrap process completes successfully without any external network connections.

Air-gapped = zero egress from any node at any stage. All artifacts are mirrored to internal infrastructure before any node is installed.

Cross-references: kubespray/kubespray-deployment.md §F (Offline image configuration), offline-artifacts/artifact-matrix.md, offline-artifacts/nexus-harbor-integration.md, compatibility/version-matrix.md.
