# Alarm list
ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl --endpoints=... alarm list

docs.title: Certificate inspection
docs.text:
# API server certificate
kubectl get -n kube-system secret <apiserver-cert-secret> -o yaml

# etcd certificates
openssl x509 -enddate -noout -in /etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/*.crt

# Controller manager certificates
ls -l /etc/kubernetes/pki/controller-manager/

docs.title: Symptoms
docs.text:
• A PVC stays Pending.
  • A pod that mounts a PVC stays in ContainerCreating with a mount error.
  • kubectl describe pvc shows ProvisioningFailed or failed to provision volume.
  • Volume expansion is rejected.
  • A snapshot exists but the restore fails.

docs.title: Likely causes
docs.text: Cause Discriminator The StorageClass does not exist or the name is wrong kubectl get storageclass The CSI provisioner pod is not running kubectl -n rook-ceph get pods -l app=rook-csi-* The CSI controller cannot reach the Ceph MON ceph -s from the CSI pod's network namespace The secrets the CSI driver needs are missing The StorageClass references a secret that does not exist The Ceph cluster is not HEALTH_OK ceph -s reports HEALTH_WARN or HEALTH_ERR The pool has no space or no free PGs ceph df, ceph osd pool ls The reclaimPolicy: Delete destroyed the PV kubectl get pv shows Released or the PV is gone Expansion not enabled The StorageClass lacks allowVolumeExpansion: true Node staging fails The node's kubelet cannot reach the OSD network

docs.title: Diagnostic commands
docs.text:
# PVC and PV state
kubectl get pvc -n <ns>
kubectl describe pvc <name> -n <ns>
kubectl get pv

# CSI driver pods
kubectl -n rook-ceph get pods -l app=rook-csi-provisioner -o wide
kubectl -n rook-ceph logs deploy/rook-csi-provisioner --tail=100
kubectl -n rook-ceph logs ds/rook-csi-nodeplugin --tail=100

# Controller logs for the specific PVC
kubectl -n rook-ceph logs deploy/rook-csi-provisioner -c csi-provisioner --tail=200 | grep -i <pvc-name>

# StorageClasses
kubectl get storageclass -o yaml
kubectl describe storageclass <sc-name>

# Ceph health from the CSI pod's viewpoint
kubectl -n rook-ceph exec deploy/rook-ceph-operator -- ceph -s
kubectl -n rook-ceph exec deploy/rook-ceph-operator -- ceph df

# Snapshot classes
kubectl get volumesnapshotclass
kubectl get volumesnapshot -n <ns>
kubectl describe volumesnapshot <name> -n <ns>

# Node-level view
lsblk
mount | grep rook
dmesg | grep -i "ceph\|blk"

docs.title: Expected healthy state
docs.text:
# kubectl get pvc
NAME       STATUS   VOLUME     CAPACITY   ACCESS MODES   STORAGECLASS   AGE
app-data   Bound    pvc-xxxx   10Gi       RWO            ceph-rbd       5m

# Ceph
HEALTH_OK
# ceph df
POOL_NAME  USED  %USED  MAX_AVAIL  OBJECTS
replicapool 1.2T  12%  8.8T       1024

docs.title: PVC stuck Pending
docs.text:
# Read the actual reason
kubectl describe pvc <name> -n <ns> | tail -20

Common causes and fixes:

Message Cause Fix no such volume / failed to provision with a CSI error The CSI controller cannot reach the cluster Check the CSI pod's network path to the MON storageclass not found Wrong StorageClass name kubectl get storageclass and correct the PVC secret "..." not found The CSI secret is missing Restore it from Vault via External Secrets rpc error: code = ResourceExhausted No space in the pool Free space or add OSDs pool ... has insufficient replicas Not enough PGs for the requested replica size Increase the number of hosts, or lower the pool replica size

docs.title: Volume expansion
docs.text:
# The StorageClass must allow it
kubectl patch storageclass ceph-rbd -p '{"allowVolumeExpansion":true}'
# Then expand the PVC
kubectl patch pvc <name> -n <ns> -p '{"spec":{"resources":{"requests":{"storage":"20Gi"}}}}'
kubectl get pvc <name> -n <ns> -w

If the expansion is rejected with "only dynamically provisioned pvc can be resized and no storageclass has allowVolumeExpansion set", the StorageClass was never patched. This is a StorageClass property, not a PVC property.

docs.title: Snapshot restore failure
docs.text:
kubectl get volumesnapshotclass
kubectl describe volumesnapshot <name> -n <ns>

# The snapshot must have a bound content
kubectl get volumesnapshotcontents

Common causes: - No VolumeSnapshotClass matching the StorageClass's deletionPolicy. - The csi.storage.k8s.io/snapshotter-secret secret is missing from the CSI namespace. - The snapshot content exists but the source volume was deleted (the snapshot becomes unusable for restore when its backing object is gone).

docs.title: Mount failure in a pod
docs.text:
# Node-side
kubectl describe pod <pod> -n <ns> | grep -A5 "Mount"
dmesg -T | grep -i ceph
kubectl -n rook-ceph logs ds/rook-csi-nodeplugin --tail=100

The node's kubelet stages the volume. If the node cannot reach the OSD ports (6800-7568), the mount hangs. Check the firewall matrix row for the storage network.

docs.title: Risks
docs.text:
• reclaimPolicy: Delete removes the PV and, with it, the Ceph image, when the PVC is deleted. Confirm before deleting a PVC.
  • A failed to delete PV can leave a Ceph image in a leaked state, consuming space. Check ceph fs ls and rbd ls for orphaned images.
  • ceph osd pool delete is irreversible and destroys data. Never run it to "clean up" a pool that a PVC still references.

docs.title: Verification after remediation
docs.text:
kubectl get pvc -A
kubectl run pvc-test --rm -it --restart=Never --image=busybox:1.36 -- \
  sh -c 'dd if=/dev/zero of=/data/test bs=1M count=100 && sync && wc -c /data/test'

Then re-run acceptance tests E-01 (dynamic provisioning), E-02 (expansion), and E-03 (snapshot and restore).

docs.title: Symptoms
docs.text:
• kubectl commands hang or fail with "no such host"
  • Pods cannot resolve service names
  • dig +short <name> returns no answer
  • curl to service DNS name fails with "Could not resolve host"

docs.title: Likely causes
docs.text:
• CoreDNS pods not running or crash-looping
  • kubelet --cluster-dns pointing to wrong address
  • /etc/resolv.conf on nodes missing cluster DNS entry
  • Network policy blocking DNS port (53/TCP, 53/UDP)
  • Upstream resolvers unreachable from cluster nodes

docs.title: Diagnostic commands
docs.text:
# Is CoreDNS running?
kubectl -n kube-system get pods -l k8s-app=kube-dns
kubectl -n kube-system logs -l k8s-app=kube-dns -c coredns

# Can we reach CoreDNS directly?
kubectl run -it --rm debug --image=registry.internal/tools/dnstools:1.0 -- \
  dig @<coredns-ip> kubernetes.default.svc.cluster.local +short

# Is node DNS config correct?
cat /etc/resolv.conf
systemctl status systemd-resolved

# Is DNS port reachable?
nc -zv <coredns-ip> 53
nc -zvu <coredns-ip> 53

# Test from inside a pod
kubectl exec -it <pod> -- cat /etc/resolv.conf
kubectl exec -it <pod> -- dig kubernetes.default.svc.cluster.local +short

docs.title: Expected healthy state
docs.text:
• CoreDNS pods: Running, 0 restarts
  • dig kubernetes.default.svc.cluster.local +short returns cluster IP
  • /etc/resolv.conf contains nameserver <cluster-dns-ip>
  • kubectl get --raw='/readyz?verbose' returns all checks ok

docs.title: Remediation
docs.text:
• Restart CoreDNS: kubectl -n kube-system rollout restart deployment/coredns
  • Fix kubelet --cluster-dns flag if nodes point to wrong address
  • Update /etc/resolv.conf on nodes if missing cluster DNS entry
  • Add network policy rule allowing DNS port 53/TCP and 53/UDP
  • Verify upstream resolvers in CoreDNS ConfigMap

docs.title: Risks
docs.text:
• Restarting CoreDNS briefly interrupts all cluster DNS resolution
  • Changing kubelet flags requires node drain and rejoin
  • Modifying /etc/resolv.conf on nodes is overwritten by cloud-init unless corrected at source

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
kubectl run -it --rm dns-test --image=registry.internal/tools/dnstools:1.0 -- \
  dig kubernetes.default.svc.cluster.local +short
kubectl run -it --rm dns-test --image=registry.internal/tools/dnstools:1.0 -- \
  dig google.com +short
kubectl get --raw='/readyz?verbose'

docs.title: Symptoms
docs.text:
• kubectl commands hang or fail with etcdserver: request timed out.
  • etcdctl endpoint health reports unhealthy members.
  • Kubernetes API writes fail while reads still work.
  • kubectl get --raw='/readyz?verbose' shows the etcd check failing.

docs.title: Likely causes
docs.text: Cause Discriminator Quorum loss (too many members down) etcdctl member list shows fewer than a quorum of healthy members Disk latency or a full disk on an etcd member df -h on the etcd data dir; etcdctl endpoint status shows a high dbSize and slow responses Clock skew between members chronyc tracking on each member Network partition between members etcdctl endpoint health from each member reports a different view Corrupted member data etcdctl alarm list shows NOSPACE or CORRUPT Certificate expiry between components openssl x509 -enddate -noout -in /etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/*.crt

docs.title: Diagnostic commands
docs.text:
# Member list and health (run on a control-plane node)
ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl \
  --endpoints=https://127.0.0.1:2379 \
  --cacert=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/ca.crt \
  --cert=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/healthcheck-client.crt \
  --key=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/healthcheck-client.key \
  member list -w table

ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl \
  --endpoints=https://127.0.0.1:2379 \
  --cacert=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/ca.crt \
  --cert=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/healthcheck-client.crt \
  --key=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/healthcheck-client.key \
  endpoint health --cluster -w table

# Endpoint status: version, db size, leader
ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl --endpoints=... endpoint status -w table

# Alarms
ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl --endpoints=... alarm list

# Slow requests logged by etcd
journalctl -u etcd --since "30 min ago" | grep -i "slow\|took too long\|apply request"

docs.title: Quorum loss
docs.text:
# Restore the down member first, then check quorum
systemctl status etcd
journalctl -u etcd -n 200

If a member's data directory is corrupted and it cannot rejoin:

# Only with the remaining quorum intact, and after taking a snapshot
ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl --endpoints=<healthy-endpoints> member remove <removed-id>
# then re-add the member from a healthy node

Removing a member is a quorum-affecting operation. Take a snapshot first and get authorization.

docs.title: NOSPACE alarm
docs.text:
df -h /var/lib/etcd
ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl --endpoints=... alarm disarm

Then free space or compact:

ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl --endpoints=... compact <revision>
ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl --endpoints=... defrag --endpoints=<one-at-a-time>

Defragment one member at a time. It blocks that member's writes while it runs.

docs.title: Clock skew
docs.text:
chronyc tracking
chronyc makestep
systemctl restart chronyd

docs.title: Last resort — restore from a snapshot
docs.text:
# Stop etcd on all members
systemctl stop etcd

ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl snapshot restore backup.db \
  --name=<member-name> \
  --initial-cluster <name1>=https://ip1:2380,name2=https://ip2:2380,name3=https://ip3:2380 \
  --initial-advertise-peer-urls https://<this-node-ip>:2380 \
  --data-dir /var/lib/etcd

Restore every member from the same snapshot, then start them one at a time and verify the leader.

docs.title: Risks
docs.text:
• member remove reduces the quorum. With 3 members, removing one leaves no tolerance for a further failure.
  • A snapshot restore loses everything written since the snapshot. State the data loss window explicitly.
  • Defragmenting all members at once removes the quorum entirely.

docs.title: Verification after remediation
docs.text:
ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl --endpoints=... endpoint health --cluster
kubectl get --raw='/readyz?verbose'
kubectl get pods -A
kubectl create job etcd-check --image=bitnami/kubectl:1.36.5 -- /bin/sh -c 'kubectl get nodes'

Then re-run acceptance test D-02 (etcd member loss, quorum maintained) if the incident involved a member failure.

docs.title: Symptoms
docs.text:
• Pipeline stuck in "pending" or "created"
  • Jobs failing with "runner not available"
  • Docker-in-Docker (DinD) failures
  • Cache not restoring between jobs
  • Artifacts not published

docs.title: Likely causes
docs.text:
• GitLab Runner not registered or offline
  • Runner tags not matching job tags
  • Docker daemon not accessible in job
  • Cache key mismatch or storage full
  • Artifact path wrong or not created

docs.title: Diagnostic commands
docs.text:
# Check runner status
gitlab-runner list
gitlab-runner status

# Check runners in GitLab
curl -H "PRIVATE-TOKEN: <token>" \
  https://<gitlab-url>/api/v4/runners

# Check job logs
# View in GitLab UI: CI/CD > Jobs > <job>

# Check runner configuration
cat /etc/gitlab-runner/config.toml

# Test Docker in runner
docker run --rm hello-world

docs.title: Expected healthy state
docs.text:
• GitLab Runner: registered, online, not paused
  • Runner tags match job tags
  • Docker daemon accessible in CI jobs
  • Cache storage available and writable
  • Artifact paths created by jobs

docs.title: Remediation
docs.text:
• Register runner: gitlab-runner register
  • Start runner: gitlab-runner start
  • Match runner tags to job tags
  • Fix Docker daemon access (mount /var/run/docker.sock)
  • Clear old cache: delete expired cache entries
  • Fix artifact paths in .gitlab-ci.yml

docs.title: Risks
docs.text:
• Unregistering runner loses all its job history
  • Restarting runner interrupts running jobs
  • Changing cache keys invalidates all existing caches

docs.title: Verification
docs.text: bash gitlab-runner list gitlab-runner verify curl -H "PRIVATE-TOKEN: <token>" \ https://<gitlab-url>/api/v4/runners?active=true | python3 -m json.tool | head -20

docs.title: Symptoms
docs.text:
• The node is not labeled nvidia.com/gpu.present=true.
  • A pod requesting nvidia.com/gpu: 1 stays Pending.
  • A pod starts but nvidia-smi inside it fails.
  • The GPU Operator pods are crash-looping.
  • A pod requests nvidia.com/gpu on a MIG-configured node and never schedules.
  • Inference pods get OOM-killed.

docs.title: Likely causes
docs.text: Cause Discriminator The driver is not installed or was built for a different kernel nvidia-smi on the host fails with "NVIDIA-SMI has failed because it couldn't communicate with the NVIDIA driver" The kernel was upgraded and the module is stale lsmod \| grep nvidia shows nothing after a kernel change The device plugin is not running kubectl -n gpu-operator get pods The container toolkit is not configured in containerd nvidia-ctk runtime configure was not run, or containerd was not restarted The pod requests the wrong resource name on a MIG GPU kubectl describe node shows MIG resources, not nvidia.com/gpu The pod has no toleration for the GPU taint The node has nvidia.com/gpu:NoSchedule The pod does not request the GPU resource The container has no nvidia.com/gpu limit VRAM exhaustion in the inference engine The vLLM log reports KV cache allocation failure

docs.title: Diagnostic commands
docs.text:
# Host state
nvidia-smi
nvidia-smi -L
nvidia-smi -q | grep -i "driver version\|mig mode"
lsmod | grep nvidia
uname -r
ls /lib/modules/
dmesg | grep -i nvidia | tail -20

# Operator state
kubectl -n gpu-operator get pods -o wide
kubectl -n gpu-operator logs -l app=nvidia-driver-daemonset --tail=100
kubectl -n gpu-operator logs -l app=nvidia-device-plugin-daemonset --tail=100
kubectl -n gpu-operator logs deploy/nvidia-operator --tail=100

# Node labels and resources
kubectl get node <gpu-node> -o jsonpath='{.metadata.labels}' | tr ',' '\n' | grep nvidia
kubectl describe node <gpu-node> | sed -n '/Allocatable/,/^Events/p'
kubectl describe node <gpu-node> | grep -i taint

# Pod scheduling
kubectl describe pod <pod> -n <ns> | grep -A10 Events

# Container runtime configuration
grep -A5 "runtimes" /etc/containerd/config.toml
cat /etc/containerd/certs.d/*/hosts.toml 2>/dev/null

# In-container check
kubectl exec -it <pod> -- nvidia-smi
kubectl exec -it <pod> -- ls -l /dev/nvidia*

docs.title: Expected healthy state
docs.text:
Host:

$ nvidia-smi
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| NVIDIA-SMI 595.71.05   Driver Version: 595.71.05   CUDA Version: 13.0     |
|   0  H100 80GB HBM3          On    |  00000000:17:00.0 Off |  0 Default |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+

Node:

$ kubectl get node <gpu-node> -o jsonpath='{.status.allocatable}' | tr ',' '\n' | grep nvidia
"nvidia.com/gpu":"8"

Pod: nvidia-smi inside the container lists exactly the GPUs the pod requested.

docs.title: The driver is missing or stale after a kernel upgrade
docs.text:
# Rebuild the module against the current kernel
sudo dkms autoinstall
sudo modprobe nvidia
nvidia-smi

On a managed node, let the GPU Operator rebuild it: drain the node, delete the driver DaemonSet pod, and let the operator recreate it.

docs.title: The container toolkit is not configured
docs.text:
sudo nvidia-ctk runtime configure --runtime=containerd --config=/etc/containerd/config.toml
sudo systemctl restart containerd

Verify the runtime section of /etc/containerd/config.toml now contains the nvidia runtime.

docs.title: The pod cannot get a GPU
docs.text:
# Check the taint and the toleration
kubectl get node <gpu-node> -o jsonpath='{.spec.taints}'

A workload that needs a GPU must have both:

tolerations:
  - key: nvidia.com/gpu
    operator: Equal
    value: "true"
    effect: NoSchedule
containers:
  - name: app
    resources:
      limits:
        nvidia.com/gpu: 1

Both are required. A toleration without the resource limit schedules on a GPU node but gets no GPU.

docs.title: MIG resource mismatch
docs.text:
kubectl describe node <gpu-node> | sed -n '/Allocatable/,/^Events/p'

If the node advertises nvidia.com/mig-1g.10gb and not nvidia.com/gpu, the request must use the MIG resource name. On a MIG-mode GPU the device plugin does not advertise a whole-GPU resource.

docs.title: GPU pod OOM-killed
docs.text:
This is usually the vLLM engine exceeding VRAM, not the pod's memory limit.

kubectl describe pod <pod> -n <ns> | grep -i "reason\|message"
kubectl logs <pod> -c vllm --previous | tail -50

Fixes, in order of effect: - Lower --gpu-memory-utilization. - Lower --max-model-len (the KV cache scales with it). - Quantize the model. - Use more GPUs with --tensor-parallel-size. - Raise the pod's memory limit if the container OOM (not the GPU) was the limit.

A pod OOM with Reason: OOMKilled and a low memory limit is a container memory issue; a vLLM error about "No available memory for the cache blocks" is a VRAM issue. They look similar in kubectl describe but are fixed differently.

docs.title: Risks
docs.text:
• Rebuilding the driver module on a node with running GPU pods interrupts them.
  • Changing the MIG profile requires the GPU to be idle, which means draining the node.
  • nvidia-smi --gpu-reset on a GPU with active compute processes fails and, in some configurations, requires the host to be rebooted.
  • A kernel upgrade on a GPU node without a matching driver build makes the GPU invisible. Always verify nvidia-smi before uncordoning.

docs.title: Verification after remediation
docs.text:
nvidia-smi
kubectl run gputest --rm -it --restart=Never \
  --image=harbor.internal/platform/cuda:<version> \
  --overrides='{"spec":{"nodeSelector":{"node-role.kubernetes.io/gpu":"true"},"containers":[{"name":"gputest","image":"harbor.internal/platform/cuda:<version>","command":["nvidia-smi"],"resources":{"limits":{"nvidia.com/gpu":1}}}]}}' \
  -- nvidia-smi

Then re-run acceptance test G-01 (GPU scheduling).

docs.title: Symptoms
docs.text:
• Users cannot log in through Keycloak
  • LDAP/AD synchronization fails
  • OIDC token validation fails
  • Group membership not reflected in Kubernetes RBAC
  • Identity provider not reachable

docs.title: Likely causes
docs.text:
• Keycloak not running or unhealthy
  • LDAP bind credentials wrong or expired
  • OIDC client configuration mismatch
  • Keycloak realm not imported or misconfigured
  • Network policy blocking LDAP/AD port (389/636)

docs.title: Diagnostic commands
docs.text:
# Is Keycloak running?
kubectl -n keycloak get pods
kubectl -n keycloak logs -l app=keycloak

# Can we reach LDAP?
ldapsearch -x -H ldap://<ldap-server> -D <bind-dn> -w <password> -b <base-dn>

# Is OIDC endpoint reachable?
curl -k https://<keycloak-url>/realms/<realm>/.well-known/openid-configuration

# Check Keycloak clients
curl -k -H "Authorization: Bearer <admin-token>" \
  https://<keycloak-url>/admin/realms/<realm>/clients

# Check user federation
kubectl -n keycloak exec <keycloak-pod> -- /opt/keycloak/bin/kcad.sh \
  get users -r <realm>

docs.title: Expected healthy state
docs.text:
• Keycloak pods: Running, 0 restarts
  • LDAP bind succeeds and returns user entries
  • OIDC well-known endpoint returns valid JSON
  • Keycloak admin API returns client list
  • User federation shows synced users

docs.title: Remediation
docs.text:
• Restart Keycloak: kubectl -n keycloak rollout restart deployment/keycloak
  • Fix LDAP bind credentials in Keycloak user federation
  • Re-import Keycloak realm configuration
  • Fix OIDC client redirect URIs and scopes
  • Add network policy allowing LDAP/AD access

docs.title: Risks
docs.text:
• Restarting Keycloak briefly interrupts all authentication
  • Wrong LDAP config can cause lockout of directory users
  • Realm misconfiguration can break SSO for all applications

docs.title: Verification
docs.text: bash kubectl -n keycloak get pods curl -k https://<keycloak-url>/realms/<realm>/.well-known/openid-configuration | python3 -m json.tool | head -5 ldapsearch -x -H ldap://<ldap-server> -D <bind-dn> -w <password> -b <base-dn> | head -5

docs.title: Symptoms
docs.text:
• Inference server not responding
  • GPU out of memory (OOM)
  • Model not loading
  • High latency / low throughput
  • Requests timing out

docs.title: Likely causes
docs.text:
• Inference server (TGI/vLLM) not running
  • GPU not allocated to workload
  • Model weights not downloaded or cached
  • Wrong GPU device visible to container
  • Concurrent requests exceeding capacity

docs.title: Diagnostic commands
docs.text:
# Is inference server running?
kubectl -n <namespace> get pods -l app=<inference-app>
kubectl -n <namespace> logs -l app=<inference-app>

# Is GPU visible?
kubectl -n <namespace> exec <pod> -- nvidia-smi
kubectl -n <namespace> exec <pod> -- cat /proc/driver/nvidia/gpus/0/information

# Is model cached?
kubectl -n <namespace> exec <pod> -- ls -la /models/
kubectl -n <namespace> exec <pod> -- ls -la /root/.cache/huggingface/

# Test inference endpoint
curl -X POST <inference-url>/v1/completions \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model": "<model>", "prompt": "Hello", "max_tokens": 10}'

# Check GPU memory
kubectl -n <namespace> exec <pod> -- nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.used,memory.total --format=csv

docs.title: Expected healthy state
docs.text:
• Inference server pods: Running, 0 restarts
  • nvidia-smi shows GPU with memory available
  • Model weights present in cache directory
  • Inference endpoint returns 200 OK
  • GPU memory usage within limits

docs.title: Remediation
docs.text:
• Restart inference server: kubectl rollout restart deployment/<inference-app>
  • Add GPU resource requests/limits to pod spec
  • Download/model cache: pre-pull model weights
  • Fix NVIDIA device plugin: kubectl get daemonset -n kube-system -l app=nvidia-device-plugin-daemonset
  • Reduce batch size or concurrent requests

docs.title: Risks
docs.text:
• Restarting inference server interrupts active requests
  • Changing GPU allocation can evict other workloads
  • Downloading large models consumes network bandwidth and storage

docs.title: Verification
docs.text: bash kubectl -n <namespace> get pods -l app=<inference-app> kubectl -n <namespace> exec <pod> -- nvidia-smi curl -sf <inference-url>/v1/models | python3 -m json.tool | head -10

docs.title: A. Purpose and scope
docs.text: Troubleshooting guide for Kubespray deployment failures. Covers Ansible connectivity, inventory validation, image pull failures, etcd bootstrap, and control-plane quorum. Cross-references kubespray-deployment.md for deployment procedures and lifecycle/upgrades/kubespray.md for upgrade procedures.

docs.title: Symptom: unreachable or failed on all hosts
docs.text:
Possible causes: - SSH key not deployed to target hosts - Wrong SSH user or port in inventory - Firewall blocking SSH (port 22) - Host not reachable from Automation Management Server

Verification: 

ansible -i inventory/<cluster>/hosts.ini all -m ping
ansible -i inventory/<cluster>/hosts.ini all -m shell -a "hostname"

Fix: - Verify SSH keys: ssh -i <key> <user>@<host> hostname - Check inventory: ansible -i inventory/<cluster>/hosts.ini all -m debug -a "var=ansible_host" - Test network: ssh -i <key> <user>@<host> -p 22 exit

docs.title: Symptom: ERROR! conflicting settings or missing variables
docs.text:
Possible causes: - group_vars/k8s_cluster/k8s-cluster.yml missing required keys - group_vars/all/all.yml missing required settings - Mixing Kubespray release group_vars without diffing

Verification: 

ansible -i inventory/<cluster>/hosts.ini all -m debug -a "var=kube_version"
ansible -i inventory/<cluster>/hosts.ini all -m debug -a "var=container_runtime"

Fix: - Diff group_vars against new release's inventory/sample - Never reuse group_vars across Kubespray releases without diffing - Pin Kubespray release in kubespray/VERSION

docs.title: D. Image pull failures in offline environment
Symptom: ImagePullBackOff or ErrImagePull on pods
docs.text:
Possible causes: - Image not mirrored to internal Harbor - containerd hosts.toml not configured for mirror - Digest mismatch between manifest and image

Verification: 

crictl inspecti <image-digest>
ctr -n k8s.io images list

Fix: - Mirror image to harbor.internal/platform/... per offline-artifacts/artifact-matrix.md - Update group_vars/all/all.yml/containerd.yml with registry mirror - Restart containerd: systemctl restart containerd

docs.title: Symptom: etcd pod crash-looping, etcd: member already exist
docs.text:
Possible causes: - Stale etcd data directory from previous deployment - Wrong etcd_deployment_type or etcd_storage_backend - Network partition between control-plane nodes

Verification: 

kubectl -n kube-system get pods -l component=etcd
kubectl -n kube-system logs -l component=etcd -c etcd

Fix: - Clean stale data directory: rm -rf /var/lib/etcd/* (on affected node only) - Verify etcd_deployment_type: stacked or external in group_vars - Restore from etcd snapshot if data is corrupted

docs.title: Symptom: kubectl get nodes returns error, API server unreachable
docs.text:
Possible causes: - Multiple control-plane nodes down simultaneously - etcd quorum lost (less than majority of members healthy) - API server static pod not recreated by kubelet

Verification: 

kubectl get nodes
kubectl get --raw='/readyz?verbose'
kubectl -n kube-system get pods -l component=kube-apiserver

Fix: - Restart one control-plane node at a time, preserving quorum - Restart kube-apiserver static pod (kubelet recreates on manifest change) - Verify kubectl auth whoami with a federated user after each restart - Do not restart all control-plane nodes simultaneously

docs.title: G. Cross-references
docs.text:
• kubespray/kubespray-deployment.md — Kubespray deployment procedures
  • lifecycle/upgrades/kubespray.md — Kubespray upgrade procedures
  • architecture/02-deployment-topology.md — Deployment topology

docs.title: Symptoms
docs.text:
• Logs not appearing in aggregation system
  • Log ingestion lagging behind real-time
  • Log parser errors (malformed JSON, missing fields)
  • Log storage full
  • Fluent Bit/Fluentd not running

docs.title: Likely causes
docs.text:
• Log collector not running on nodes
  • Wrong log paths in configuration
  • Parser regex not matching log format
  • Backend storage (Elasticsearch/Loki) unreachable
  • Buffer overflow (too many logs, slow backend)

docs.title: Diagnostic commands
docs.text:
# Is log collector running?
kubectl -n logging get pods -l app=fluent-bit
kubectl -n logging logs -l app=fluent-bit

# Check log files exist
ls -la /var/log/<app>/
ls -la /var/log/pods/

# Check parser configuration
kubectl -n logging get configmap fluent-bit-config -o yaml

# Check backend connectivity
kubectl -n logging exec <fluent-bit-pod> -- curl -sf <backend-url>/api/health

# Check buffer status
kubectl -n logging exec <fluent-bit-pod> -- fluent-bit -c /fluent-bit/etc/fluent-bit.conf -R

# Check pod logs directly
kubectl logs <pod> -n <namespace> --tail=50

docs.title: Expected healthy state
docs.text:
• Fluent Bit/Fluentd daemonset: All pods Running
  • Log files present at expected paths
  • Parser configuration valid (no errors on startup)
  • Backend reachable and accepting logs
  • No buffer overflow warnings

docs.title: Remediation
docs.text:
• Restart log collector: kubectl -n logging rollout restart daemonset/fluent-bit
  • Fix log paths in configuration
  • Fix parser regex to match actual log format
  • Fix backend connectivity (network, authentication)
  • Increase buffer size or reduce log volume

docs.title: Risks
docs.text:
• Restarting log collector causes brief log gap
  • Wrong parser config can cause all logs to be dropped
  • Increasing buffer uses more disk/memory on nodes

docs.title: Verification
docs.text: bash kubectl -n logging get pods -l app=fluent-bit kubectl -n logging logs -l app=fluent-bit --tail=20 | grep -i error kubectl logs <pod> -n <namespace> --tail=10

docs.title: Symptoms
docs.text:
• Pods cannot communicate across nodes
  • Service endpoints not reachable
  • ping -c3 <target-ip> returns 100% loss
  • nc -zv <target> <port> connection refused or timeout
  • curl -vk https://<target> hangs

docs.title: Likely causes
docs.text:
• CNI plugin not running or misconfigured
  • Network policy blocking traffic
  • Security group or firewall rules dropping packets
  • MTU mismatch between overlay and underlay
  • Node IP not in pod CIDR range
  • IP forwarding disabled on nodes

docs.title: Diagnostic commands
docs.text:
# Layer 3: Is target reachable at all?
ping -c3 <target-ip>

# Layer 4: Is port open?
nc -zv <target> <port>

# Layer 5/7: Is service responding?
curl -vk https://<target>

# CNI status
kubectl get daemonset -n kube-system -l k8s-app=cilium
kubectl -n kube-system logs -l k8s-app=cilium -c cilium-agent

# Node IP forwarding
cat /proc/sys/net/ipv4/ip_forward

# MTU
ip link show | grep mtu
ip route show

# Network policies
kubectl get networkpolicy -A

# Routes
ip route get <target-ip>

docs.title: Expected healthy state
docs.text:
• ping -c3 <target-ip> returns 0% loss
  • nc -zv <target> <port> reports "Connection succeeded"
  • ip_forward = 1 on all nodes
  • CNI daemonset pods all Running
  • No network policies blocking the path

docs.title: Remediation
docs.text:
• Restart CNI daemonset: kubectl -n kube-system rollout restart daemonset/cilium
  • Fix network policy rules blocking the traffic
  • Update security group/firewall rules
  • Correct MTU mismatch (lower overlay MTU to match underlay)
  • Enable IP forwarding: sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_forward=1
  • Verify node IP is within configured pod CIDR

docs.title: Risks
docs.text:
• Changing MTU can cause temporary connectivity loss
  • Removing network policies exposes services to unintended traffic
  • Changing firewall rules can lock out management access

docs.title: Verification
docs.text: bash ping -c3 <target-ip> nc -zv <target> <port> curl -sf https://<target> && echo "OK" kubectl get --raw='/readyz?verbose'

docs.title: Symptoms
docs.text:
• skopeo copy fails with "manifest unknown" or "unauthorized"
  • apt or dnf cannot find packages in offline repository
  • Helm chart installation fails: "chart not found"
  • Docker/containerd image pull fails in air-gapped environment
  • Python pip cannot install from offline index

docs.title: Likely causes
docs.text:
• Image not mirrored to internal registry
  • Repository metadata out of sync
  • Missing artifact in offline-artifacts/artifact-matrix.md
  • Registry authentication not configured
  • Network policy blocking registry access

docs.title: Diagnostic commands
docs.text:
# Check if image exists in registry
skopeo inspect docker://registry.internal/platform/<image>:<tag>

# Check artifact matrix
cat offline-artifacts/artifact-matrix.md | grep <artifact-name>

# Check containerd images
crictl inspecti <image-digest>
ctr -n k8s.io images list | grep <image>

# Check apt/dnf repositories
apt-cache policy <package>
dnf repoinfo <repo>

# Check Helm charts
helm search repo <chart-name>

# Test registry authentication
skopeo inspect --creds <user>:<pass> docker://registry.internal/platform/<image>:<tag>

docs.title: Expected healthy state
docs.text:
• All required images present in internal registry
  • skopeo inspect succeeds for all pinned images
  • Artifact matrix lists all dependencies with versions
  • Repository metadata current (repodata/repomd.xml present)
  • Helm charts indexed and installable

docs.title: Remediation
docs.text:
• Mirror missing images per offline-artifacts/artifact-matrix.md
  • Sync repository metadata: reposync or apt-mirror
  • Update artifact matrix with new dependency versions
  • Configure registry authentication in containerd (hosts.toml)
  • Add network policy allowing registry access

docs.title: Risks
docs.text:
• Mirroring large images consumes significant storage
  • Out-of-sync repository metadata can cause dependency resolution failures
  • Wrong registry credentials can cause widespread pull failures

docs.title: Verification
docs.text: bash skopeo inspect docker://registry.internal/platform/<image>:<tag> ctr -n k8s.io images list | grep <image> cat offline-artifacts/artifact-matrix.md | grep <artifact-name>

docs.title: Symptoms
docs.text:
• apt or dnf returns "Unable to locate package"
  • Package installation fails with dependency conflicts
  • apt-get update fails with GPG signature errors
  • Repository metadata out of date
  • Lock file held by another process

docs.title: Likely causes
docs.text:
• Repository not configured or unreachable
  • GPG key expired or missing
  • Package cache corrupted
  • Lock file from previous process
  • Wrong distribution version in sources list

docs.title: Diagnostic commands
docs.text:
# Check apt/dnf status
apt-cache policy <package>
dnf repoinfo <package>

# Check repository configuration
cat /etc/apt/sources.list.d/*.list
cat /etc/yum.repos.d/*.repo

# Check GPG keys
apt-key list
rpm -q gpg-pubkey

# Check for lock files
ls /var/lib/apt/lists/lock /var/lib/dnf/lock 2>/dev/null
ps aux | grep -E "apt|dnf|yum"

# Clear cache
apt-get clean
dnf clean all

docs.title: Expected healthy state
docs.text:
• apt-cache policy <package> shows candidate version
  • dnf repoinfo <package> shows available version
  • No lock files held by other processes
  • Repository metadata current (not stale)
  • GPG keys present and valid

docs.title: Remediation
docs.text:
• Refresh package index: apt-get update or dnf makecache
  • Import missing GPG keys: apt-key adv --keyserver ... or rpm --import
  • Remove stale lock files: rm -f /var/lib/apt/lists/lock
  • Kill stale apt/dnf processes and retry
  • Fix repository URLs in sources list

docs.title: Risks
docs.text:
• Removing lock files while another process runs can corrupt package database
  • Importing wrong GPG keys can allow untrusted packages
  • Changing repository URLs can pull packages from unintended sources

docs.title: Verification
docs.text: bash apt-get update apt-cache policy <package> dnf makecache dnf repoinfo <package>

docs.title: Symptoms
docs.text:
• Prometheus targets show "down" in targets page
  • No metrics being scraped
  • Alertmanager not receiving alerts
  • Prometheus disk usage growing unbounded
  • Query performance degraded

docs.title: Likely causes
docs.text:
• Scrape config pointing to wrong targets
  • ServiceMonitor not configured correctly
  • Target pods not exposing /metrics endpoint
  • Prometheus storage retention too long
  • Query too heavy (too many labels, too long range)

docs.title: Diagnostic commands
docs.text:
# Is Prometheus running?
kubectl -n monitoring get pods -l app=prometheus
kubectl -n monitoring logs -l app=prometheus

# Check targets
curl -s http://<prometheus-url>/api/v1/targets | python3 -m json.tool

# Check ServiceMonitors
kubectl get servicemonitor -A

# Check scrape config
kubectl -n monitoring get prometheus -o yaml | grep -A20 scrape_configs

# Check disk usage
kubectl -n monitoring exec <prometheus-pod> -- df -h /prometheus

# Check target health
curl -sf http://<target-ip>:<metrics-port>/metrics | head -5

docs.title: Expected healthy state
docs.text:
• Prometheus pods: Running, 0 restarts
  • All targets: "up" in /api/v1/targets
  • ServiceMonitors: bound to correct services
  • /metrics endpoint returns Prometheus-format metrics
  • Disk usage within retention limits

docs.title: Remediation
docs.text:
• Fix scrape configuration targets
  • Create/fix ServiceMonitor resources
  • Ensure pods expose /metrics endpoint on correct port
  • Reduce retention time: --storage.tsdb.retention.time=15d
  • Optimize queries (reduce label cardinality, shorter ranges)

docs.title: Risks
docs.text:
• Changing scrape config can cause temporary metric gaps
  • Reducing retention loses historical data
  • Heavy queries can impact Prometheus performance

docs.title: Verification
docs.text: bash curl -s http://<prometheus-url>/api/v1/targets | python3 -c " import json,sys d=json.load(sys.stdin) for t in d['data']['activeTargets']: print(t['discoveredLabels']['job'], t['health']) " kubectl get servicemonitor -A

docs.title: Symptoms
docs.text:
• Rancher UI not reachable
  • Cluster registration fails
  • Fleet jobs not deploying
  • Catalog entries not available
  • Authentication failures (Keycloak integration)

docs.title: Likely causes
docs.text:
• Rancher deployment not running
  • Cluster agent not connected
  • Fleet controller not running
  • Helm chart repository not synced
  • Keycloak OIDC misconfiguration

docs.title: Diagnostic commands
docs.text:
# Is Rancher running?
kubectl -n cattle-system get pods
kubectl -n cattle-system logs -l app=rancher

# Is cluster agent connected?
kubectl -n cattle-system get pods -l app=cattle-cluster-agent
kubectl -n cattle-system logs -l app=cattle-cluster-agent

# Is Fleet running?
kubectl -n cattle-fleet-system get pods
kubectl -n cattle-fleet-system logs -l app=fleet-controller

# Is Keycloak reachable?
kubectl -n keycloak get pods
kubectl -n keycloak logs -l app=keycloak

# Check Rancher API
curl -k https://<rancher-url>/v3/

docs.title: Expected healthy state
docs.text:
• Rancher deployment: Available, 1+ replicas
  • Cluster agent: Running, connected to server
  • Fleet controller: Running
  • Keycloak: Running, healthy
  • curl -k https://<rancher-url>/v3/ returns JSON

docs.title: Remediation
docs.text:
• Restart Rancher: kubectl -n cattle-system rollout restart deployment/rancher
  • Re-register cluster: generate new cluster registration token
  • Restart Fleet: kubectl -n cattle-fleet-system rollout restart deployment/fleet-controller
  • Sync Helm repositories: helm repo update
  • Fix Keycloak OIDC client configuration in Rancher

docs.title: Risks
docs.text:
• Restarting Rancher briefly makes management UI unavailable
  • Re-registering cluster requires cluster-admin access
  • Wrong Keycloak config can lock out all users

docs.title: Verification
docs.text: bash kubectl -n cattle-system get deployment rancher kubectl -n cattle-fleet-system get deployment fleet-controller curl -sf https://<rancher-url>/v3/ && echo "OK"

docs.title: Symptoms
docs.text:
• crictl pull fails with unauthorized: authentication required.
  • ImagePullBackOff on a pod.
  • helm install fails with a 401 or 403 from the chart repository.
  • apt-get update fails with NO_PUBKEY or The repository ... is not signed.
  • dnf install fails with GPG check FAILED.
  • pip install fails with a TLS verification error.
  • A push to Harbor fails with denied: requested access to the resource is denied.

docs.title: Likely causes
docs.text: Cause Discriminator The registry credentials are not in the containerd configuration /etc/containerd/certs.d/<registry>/hosts.toml has no Authorization header The CA is not in the containerd trust store The error mentions an unknown authority or certificate The Harbor project does not exist curl -k -u user:pass https://harbor/api/v2.0/projects/<name> returns 404 The robot account lacks the pull or push permission The push returns 403 with a policy message The image path does not exist in the internal registry The pull returns manifest unknown The image was mirrored to a different repository path The pull returns repository not found The package repository's GPG key is missing NO_PUBKEY or GPG check FAILED The repository's Release file is not signed correctly apt reports the repository is not signed The Nexus/Harbor URL is wrong or the path layout differs 404 on the repository path

docs.title: Diagnostic commands
docs.text:
# containerd
crictl pull harbor.internal/platform/app:1.0.0
crictl images | head
ctr -n k8s.io images ls | head

# The containerd registry config
cat /etc/containerd/certs.d/harbor.internal/hosts.toml
systemctl status containerd
journalctl -u containerd --since "5 min ago" | tail -30

# Harbor API
curl -sk -u "$ROBO_USER:$ROBO_PASS" https://harbor.internal/api/v2.0/projects | jq '.[].name'
curl -sk -u "$ROBO_USER:$ROBO_PASS" \
  "https://harbor.internal/v2/platform/app/tags/list" | jq .

# Nexus
curl -sk -u "$NEXUS_USER:$NEXUS_PASS" https://nexus.internal/service/rest/v1/status
curl -skI https://nexus.internal/repository/deb-ubuntu/dists/noble/InRelease

# apt
apt-get update -o Debug::Acquire::http=true
apt-cache policy <package>

# dnf
dnf repolist --enabled
dnf install --downloadonly --downloaddir=/tmp/dnf-test <package>
rpm -qa gpg-pubkey --qf '%{name}-%{version} %{summary}\n'

# pip
pip config list
pip download --no-deps --dest /tmp/piptest requests

docs.title: Expected healthy state
docs.text:
$ crictl pull harbor.internal/platform/app:1.0.0
1f2e3d4c5b6a@sha256:abc123...

$ apt-get update
Hit:1 https://nexus.internal/repository/deb-ubuntu noble InRelease

docs.title: containerd cannot pull from the internal registry
docs.text:
The hosts.toml for the registry must contain the CA path, the credentials, and the mirror endpoint:

# /etc/containerd/certs.d/harbor.internal/hosts.toml
server = "https://harbor.internal"

[host."https://harbor.internal"]
  capabilities = ["pull", "resolve"]
  ca = "/etc/containerd/certs.d/harbor.internal/ca.crt"
  skip_verify = false
  [host."https://harbor.internal".header]
    Authorization = "Basic <base64 user:password>"

Then restart containerd:

systemctl restart containerd

Credentials in this file are a secret. In this platform the file is written by Ansible from a Vault lookup, and the robot account secret is rotated on a schedule.

docs.title: Harbor project missing or the permission is wrong
docs.text:
curl -sk -u "$ADMIN_USER:$ADMIN_PASS" -X POST \
  https://harbor.internal/api/v2.0/projects \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"project_name":"platform","public":false,"registry_id":0}'

Robot account permissions are set on the project. A pull-only robot account cannot push; the push failure says denied: requested access to the resource is denied.

docs.title: The image was mirrored to the wrong path
docs.text:
The rule that avoids this: mirror with the same repository path as upstream. ghcr.io/owner/app becomes harbor.internal/owner/app, not harbor.internal/platform/app. When the paths match, no manifest rewrite is needed anywhere and the image list is mechanical.

If the paths genuinely differ, every consumer needs a rewrite rule — Argo CD image rewrite, Kubespray *_image_repo overrides, and the Dockerfile FROM lines. That is why the matching-path rule exists.

docs.title: apt/dnf GPG failure
docs.text:
# Import the internal repository key
curl -fsSL https://nexus.internal/repository/deb-ubuntu/keys/internal.gpg \
  | gpg --dearmor -o /usr/share/keyrings/internal-nexus.gpg
apt-get update

rpm --import https://nexus.internal/repository/rpm-oraclelinux/keys/ol9.key
dnf makecache

docs.title: The CA is not trusted by containerd
docs.text:
containerd does not use the system trust store for registry TLS by default when certs.d is in use. The ca key in hosts.toml points at the CA file. If ca is omitted, containerd falls back to the system store.

cp internal-ca.crt /etc/containerd/certs.d/harbor.internal/ca.crt
systemctl restart containerd

docs.title: pip TLS failure
docs.text:
# /etc/pip.conf or the venv pip.conf
[global]
index-url = https://nexus.internal/repository/pypi/simple
extra-index-url =
trusted-host =
cert = /etc/pki/ca-trust/source/anchors/internal-ca.crt

Never set trusted-host as a workaround for a certificate error. That disables verification for that host.

docs.title: Risks
docs.text:
• skip_verify = true in the containerd registry config disables TLS verification for that registry. Use it only temporarily to isolate a CA distribution problem.
  • Deleting and recreating a Harbor project deletes the images in it.
  • Rotating a robot account secret requires updating containerd on every node and restarting containerd. During that window, image pulls fail on the restarted nodes. Rotate in a controlled rolling fashion.

docs.title: Verification after remediation
docs.text:
# On every node
crictl pull harbor.internal/platform/app:1.0.0
# Offline environment
kubectl run pulltest --rm -it --restart=Never \
  --image=harbor.internal/platform/busybox:1.36 -- echo pull-ok

Then re-run acceptance tests F-01 (offline package install) and F-02 (offline image pull).

docs.title: Universal First-Response Sequence
docs.text:
Run this before any component-specific procedure. It eliminates most misdiagnoses.

# 1. Is the problem in my session or in the system?
date; timedatectl  # skew?

# 2. Is the target reachable at all?
ping -c 3 <target-ip>        # layer 3
nc -zv <target> <port>       # layer 4
curl -vk https://<target>    # layer 5/7

# 3. Is the service actually running?
systemctl status <unit> --no-pager
kubectl get pods -A | grep -v Running
kubectl get events -A --sort-by=.lastTimestamp | tail -30

# 4. Is it the cluster, or the workload?
kubectl get --raw='/readyz?verbose'
kubectl describe node <node>

docs.title: Severity Classification (SLO-driven)
docs.text: Severity Error Budget Impact Escalation Trigger P0 Critical >50% budget consumed in 1h Auto-escalate to on-call lead P1 High >50% budget consumed in 6h Escalate after 2h if no progress P2 Medium 20-50% budget consumed Review at next standup P3 Low <20% budget consumed Log and track

docs.title: Blameless Post-Incident Review Template
docs.text:
• What happened: Timeline of events
  • Impact: Users affected, error budget consumed
  • Root cause: Systemic failure, not human error
  • Fix: Change that prevents recurrence
  • Action items: Owners, deadlines, verification
  • Prevention: Process or automation improvement

docs.title: DNS Resolution Failures
docs.text:
• Symptoms: kubectl hangs, dig returns no answer, curl fails with "no such host"
  • Likely causes: CoreDNS not running, wrong cluster DNS, /etc/resolv.conf misconfig, network policy blocking port 53
  • See: troubleshooting/dns.md for full runbook

docs.title: TLS/Certificate Expiry
docs.text:
• Symptoms: curl returns cert errors, browsers show "certificate expired", service returns 502/503
  • Likely causes: Certificate expiry, mismatched hostname, chain incomplete, clock skew
  • See: troubleshooting/tls.md for full runbook

docs.title: etcd Performance Degradation
docs.text:
• Symptoms: kubectl slow, API responses delayed, backup times out
  • Likely causes: Disk pressure, WAL blooming, too many etcd members, snapshot failures
  • See: troubleshooting/etcd.md for full runbook

docs.title: Kubernetes API Server Issues
docs.text:
• Symptoms: kubectl get timeout, pods stuck in Pending, health checks failing
  • Likely causes: apiserver resource pressure, certificate expiry, RBAC misconfig, network policies
  • See: troubleshooting/apiserver.md for full runbook

docs.title: Node Resource Pressure
docs.text:
• Symptoms: Pods scheduled but not running, OOMKilled, disk pressure errors
  • Likely causes: Memory leak, log rotation failure, disk full, node auto-scaler not triggering
  • See: troubleshooting/kubespray.md for full runbook

docs.title: Service Mesh Routing Failures
docs.text:
• Symptoms: Traffic not routed, mTLS handshake failures, retries not respecting circuit breaker
  • Likely causes: Sidecar proxy misconfig, cert expiry in mesh, policy mismatch, pilot-agent disconnect
  • See: troubleshooting/service-mesh.md for full runbook

docs.title: GPU Driver and Device Allocation Failures
docs.text:
• Symptoms: Pods pending with " insufficient nodes", devices not visible, out-of-memory on GPU
  • Likely causes: Driver version mismatch, device plugin not running, CUDA runtime mismatch, MIG config errors
  • See: troubleshooting/gpu.md for full runbook

docs.title: LLM Inference and GPU Memory Exhaustion
docs.text:
• Symptoms: Generation stalls, OOM errors, model load fails, token throughput drops
  • Likely causes: GPU memory fragmentation, model too large for device, concurrency too high, thermal throttling
  • See: troubleshooting/inference.md for full runbook

docs.title: Backup and Recovery Failures
docs.text:
• Symptoms: Backup job fails, restore takes longer than RTO, data loss detected, snapshot stuck
  • Likely causes: Storage capacity, network timeout, encryption key rotation, incompatible client version
  • See: troubleshooting/backup-restore.md for full runbook

docs.title: Layer 1: Physical/Infrastructure
docs.text: Check Command Healthy State Node reachability ping -c 3 <ip> 0% loss Port reachability nc -zv <ip> <port> Connection succeeded Disk health df -h <80% usage Node status kubectl get nodes Ready status BIOS/time sync timedatectl NTP synchronized, offset < 100ms

docs.title: Layer 2: Network
docs.text: Check Command Healthy State Name resolution dig +short <name> Returns expected IP Reverse DNS dig -x <ip> Returns expected hostname TLS handshake openssl s_client -connect <ip>:443 -servername <name> Verify return code 0, correct chain Service port nc -z <ip> <port> Connection succeeded Mesh traffic istioctl proxy-config endpoints <pod> Endpoints listed

docs.title: Layer 3: Service/Kubernetes
docs.text: Check Command Healthy State Pod status kubectl get pods -o wide Running, 0 restarts Readiness kubectl get --raw='/readyz?verbose' All checks ok Events kubectl describe pod <pod> No recent warnings Logs (previous) kubectl logs <pod> --previous Previous output (crash loops) Service IP kubectl get svc <svc> -o wide ClusterIP assigned Network policy kubectl get networkpolicy Expected rules present

docs.title: Layer 4: Application
docs.text: Check Command Healthy State Readiness probe curl -s <pod-ip>:<port>/ready 200 OK Liveness probe curl -s <pod-ip>:<port>/live 200 OK Metrics endpoint curl -s <pod-ip>:<port>/metrics Returns prometheus format Health summary kubectl get --raw='/api/v1/namespaces/<ns>/pods/<pod>/proxy/healthz' 200 OK

docs.title: Pre-Deployment Checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] Error budget sufficient for risk level (see SLO framework)
  • [ ] Canary deployment at 5% for 15 min, then 25% for 30 min
  • [ ] Rollback plan documented and tested
  • [ ] Feature flags configured for new pathways
  • [ ] Monitoring alerts verified firing correctly
  • [ ] Log aggregation path verified (new service shipper configured)
  • [ ] Traces configured with correct service name
  • [ ] Resource limits reviewed and applied
  • [ ] Security context reviewed (privilege escalation check)
  • [ ] Secrets mounted read-only where possible

docs.title: Post-Deployment Verification
docs.text:
• [ ] SLO within target after warmup period (5m for critical, 30m for high)
  • [ ] Error budget consumption rate stable or decreasing
  • [ ] Key metrics returned to baseline
  • [ ] No new alert firings in last 10m
  • [ ] Canary traffic at 100% with healthy metrics
  • [ ] Rollback window closed if all checks pass

docs.title: Daily Cluster Health Checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] All nodes Ready: kubectl get nodes --no-headers | grep -c Ready equals total nodes
  • [ ] No NotReady nodes: kubectl get nodes output shows 0/ Ready
  • [ ] CoreDNS healthy: kubectl -n kube-system get pods -l k8s-app=kube-dns all Running
  • [ ] etcd metrics within bounds: kubectl exec -n kube-system <etcd-pod> -- etcdctl endpoint status -w table
  • [ ] API server latency < 50ms p99: kubectl get --raw='/livez'
  • [ ] No pending pods with default QoS: kubectl get pods --all-namespaces | grep Pending | grep -v "qos=best-effort"
  • [ ] Storage available: kubectl get pvc --all-namespaces all Bound
  • [ ] Security scans passed: verify new images against registry scan

docs.title: Weekly Reliability Review Checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] Error budget burn rate analyzed over 30d window
  • [ ] SLO targets reviewed for relevance (user experience alignment)
  • [ ] Automation opportunities identified (toil > 4h/week)
  • [ ] Chaos experiment results reviewed and incorporated
  • [ ] Dependency versions checked for security advisories
  • [ ] Capacity planning data reviewed (CPU/mem trends 30/60/90d)
  • [ ] Runbook currency verified (all links valid, last tested < 30d ago)
  • [ ] Post-incident action items closed or scheduled

docs.title: Monthly Infrastructure Review Checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] Node autoscaler policies reviewed and adjusted
  • [ ] Storage capacity forecast and provisioning
  • [ ] Certificate expiry dates checked (30/60/90d windows)
  • [ ] Backup and restore time tested in staging
  • [ ] Disaster recovery runbook reviewed and updated
  • [ ] Cost optimization opportunities documented
  • [ ] Security policy updates applied
  • [ ] SLO targets adjusted based on user pattern changes

docs.title: Risks and Mitigation
docs.text: Risk Mitigation Runbook out of date Schedule monthly currency review; auto-link check with scripts/check_links.py Remediation makes things worse Collect evidence before any destructive action; one change at a time Escalation delay Pre-defined escalation paths with on-call rotas; SLO-driven severity Alert fatigue Quarterly alert review; silence thresholds based on error budget Common failure mode not documented Post-incident: always add to runbook within 48h of resolution

docs.title: Link Validation
docs.text:
Run the link checker to verify all internal references:

python3 scripts/check_links.py

Expected: 0 broken links. Any output indicates missing files or dead anchors that should be fixed.

docs.title: Symptoms
docs.text:
• Pods cannot mount secrets
  • Vault agent injector fails to inject secrets
  • Secret not found at expected path
  • Authentication to Vault fails
  • Secret rotation not propagating to running pods

docs.title: Likely causes
docs.text:
• Vault not running or sealed
  • Kubernetes auth method not configured
  • Secret path wrong or not created
  • Vault agent sidecar crash-looping
  • Secret CSI driver not installed

docs.title: Diagnostic commands
docs.text:
# Is Vault running?
kubectl -n vault get pods
kubectl -n vault logs -l app=vault

# Is Vault sealed?
vault status

# Can we authenticate?
vault login -method=kubernetes role=<role>
vault token lookup

# Check secret exists
vault kv get <path>

# Check CSI driver
kubectl get daemonset -n vault-csi -l app=vault-secret-csi-driver

# Check pod events
kubectl describe pod <pod> | grep -A5 "Events"

docs.title: Expected healthy state
docs.text:
• Vault: Unsealed, healthy
  • vault token lookup returns valid token info
  • vault kv get <path> returns secret data
  • Secret CSI driver daemonset: Running
  • Pod events show successful secret mount

docs.title: Remediation
docs.text:
• Unseal Vault: vault operator unseal with 3 keys
  • Restart Vault: kubectl -n vault rollout restart sts/vault
  • Configure Kubernetes auth method: vault write auth/kubernetes/config
  • Create secret at correct path: vault kv put <path> key=value
  • Install Secret CSI driver if missing

docs.title: Risks
docs.text:
• Unsealing Vault requires 3 separate key holders
  • Restarting Vault briefly interrupts all secret access
  • Wrong auth config can lock out all applications

docs.title: Verification
docs.text: bash vault status vault token lookup vault kv get <path> kubectl describe pod <pod> | grep -A3 "secret"

docs.title: Symptoms
docs.text:
• Sidecar injection not working
  • mTLS between services failing
  • Traffic not routing correctly
  • Istio control plane not healthy
  • Gateway not receiving external traffic

docs.title: Likely causes
docs.text:
• Istio sidecar injector not running
  • DestinationRule missing or wrong
  • VirtualService not matching traffic
  • Istiod not running or unhealthy
  • Gateway not configured for correct ports

docs.title: Diagnostic commands
docs.text:
# Is Istiod running?
kubectl -n istio-system get pods -l app=istiod
kubectl -n istio-system logs -l app=istiod

# Is sidecar injector working?
kubectl get pod <pod> -o jsonpath='{.spec.containers[*].name}' | grep istio-proxy

# Check DestinationRules
kubectl get destinationrule -A

# Check VirtualServices
kubectl get virtualservice -A

# Check Gateways
kubectl get gateway -A

# Test sidecar proxy
kubectl exec <pod> -c istio-proxy -- pilot-agent request GET server_info

docs.title: Expected healthy state
docs.text:
• Istiod: Running, healthy
  • Sidecar injected into workload pods
  • DestinationRules exist for all services
  • VirtualServices route traffic correctly
  • Gateways configured for correct ports

docs.title: Remediation
docs.text:
• Enable sidecar injection: kubectl label namespace <ns> istio-injection=enabled
  • Restart pods to get sidecar: kubectl rollout restart deployment/<app>
  • Create/fix DestinationRules
  • Create/fix VirtualServices
  • Restart Istiod: kubectl -n istio-system rollout restart deployment/istiod

docs.title: Risks
docs.text:
• Enabling sidecar injection restarts all pods in namespace
  • Wrong VirtualService can misroute traffic
  • Removing Gateway can cut off external access

docs.title: Verification
docs.text: bash kubectl -n istio-system get pods -l app=istiod kubectl get destinationrule -A kubectl get virtualservice -A kubectl get gateway -A kubectl exec <pod> -c istio-proxy -- curl -sf localhost:15000/server_info

docs.title: Symptoms
docs.text:
• timedatectl shows large offset or "System clock synchronized: no"
  • TLS certificate validation fails (certificate not yet valid / expired)
  • Kubernetes API rejects requests with timestamp skew errors
  • etcd cluster members cannot agree on leader
  • Logs show timestamps out of order

docs.title: Likely causes
docs.text:
• chronyd or systemd-timesyncd not running
  • NTP servers unreachable from nodes
  • Hardware clock drift
  • VM host time not synchronized (virtualized environments)
  • Timezone mismatch between nodes

docs.title: Diagnostic commands
docs.text:
# Check time synchronization status
timedatectl
chronyc tracking
chronyc sources -v

# Check offset
chronyc tracking | grep "Last offset"

# Compare across nodes
for host in <node-list>; do ssh $host "date -u && timedatectl"; done

# Check NTP reachability
nc -zv <ntp-server> 123

# Check hardware clock
hwclock --debug

docs.title: Expected healthy state
docs.text:
• timedatectl shows "System clock synchronized: yes"
  • chronyc tracking shows "Leap status: normal"
  • Offset < 100 ms
  • All nodes within 1 second of each other

docs.title: Remediation
docs.text:
• Start and enable chronyd: systemctl enable --now chronyd
  • Verify NTP servers in /etc/chrony.conf or /etc/systemd/timesyncd.conf
  • Restart chronyd after config change: systemctl restart chronyd
  • Force sync: chronyc burst <ntp-server>
  • Check VM host time if running in virtualized environment

docs.title: Risks
docs.text:
• Large time jumps can break TLS sessions and Kubernetes API tokens
  • Restarting time sync service briefly disrupts time-sensitive operations
  • Hardware clock drift may indicate failing CMOS battery or host issue

docs.title: Verification
docs.text: bash timedatectl | grep "System clock synchronized" chronyc tracking | grep -E "Leap status|Last offset" for host in <node-list>; do ssh $host "date -u +%s"; done | sort -n | uniq -c

docs.title: Symptoms
docs.text:
• openssl s_client returns verification failure
  • Kubernetes API rejects client certificates
  • Pods fail with "x509: certificate has expired"
  • cert-manager certificates stuck in Pending
  • mTLS handshake failures between services

docs.title: Likely causes
docs.text:
• Certificate expired or not yet valid
  • CA chain incomplete or wrong
  • Wrong certificate for the hostname (SAN mismatch)
  • Clock skew between client and server
  • Private key doesn't match certificate
  • Intermediate CA missing from chain

docs.title: Diagnostic commands
docs.text:
# Verify certificate
openssl x509 -in <cert.pem> -text -noout
openssl verify -CAfile <ca.pem> <cert.pem>

# Test TLS connection
openssl s_client -connect <host>:443 -servername <name>
openssl s_client -connect <host>:443 -showcerts

# Check certificate dates
openssl x509 -in <cert.pem> -noout -dates

# Check SANs
openssl x509 -in <cert.pem> -noout -ext subjectAltName

# Verify key matches cert
openssl x509 -noout -modulus -in <cert.pem> | openssl md5
openssl rsa -noout -modulus -in <key.pem> | openssl md5

# Check clock
date -u

docs.title: Expected healthy state
docs.text:
• Certificate valid (not expired, not yet valid)
  • openssl verify returns "OK"
  • openssl s_client returns verify return code 0
  • Key modulus matches certificate modulus
  • Clock within 5 minutes of server time

docs.title: Remediation
docs.text:
• Renew expired certificate
  • Add missing intermediate CA to chain
  • Reissue certificate with correct SANs
  • Fix clock skew (see troubleshooting/time.md)
  • Re-generate key/cert pair if mismatch
  • Update trust store with correct CA

docs.title: Risks
docs.text:
• Renewing certificates can briefly break existing TLS connections
  • Wrong CA in trust store can cause widespread verification failures
  • Removing expired CA can break legacy systems still using it

docs.title: Verification
docs.text: bash openssl verify -CAfile <ca.pem> <cert.pem> openssl s_client -connect <host>:443 -servername <name> </dev/null 2>&1 | grep "Verify return code" date -u

docs.title: Symptoms
docs.text:
• Control-plane upgrade fails mid-way
  • Worker nodes not joining after upgrade
  • Kubespray playbook fails on upgrade task
  • Pods evicted during upgrade
  • Version mismatch between control-plane and workers

docs.title: Likely causes
docs.text:
• Kubespray version incompatible with target Kubernetes version
  • Control-plane upgraded before etcd
  • Worker nodes drained but not uncordoned
  • Image not available for new version
  • etcd snapshot not taken before upgrade

docs.title: Diagnostic commands
docs.text:
# Check version consistency
kubectl get nodes -o wide | grep -E "VERSION|STATUS"
kubectl version --short

# Check Kubespray version
cat kubespray/VERSION

# Check playbook run status
# Review ansible-playbook output log

# Check node conditions
kubectl get nodes -o json | jq '.items[] | {name: .metadata.name, conditions: .status.conditions}'

# Check etcd health
etcdctl --endpoints=https://127.0.0.1:2379 endpoint health --cluster

docs.title: Expected healthy state
docs.text:
• All nodes: Ready, same or compatible version
  • etcd: healthy quorum
  • Kubespray version matches deployment (release-2.32)
  • No nodes in NotReady state after upgrade

docs.title: Remediation
docs.text:
• Match Kubespray version to target Kubernetes version
  • Upgrade control-plane nodes one at a time
  • Upgrade etcd before API server
  • Uncordon worker nodes after upgrade completes
  • Take etcd snapshot before any upgrade

docs.title: Risks
docs.text:
• Upgrading all control-plane nodes simultaneously removes quorum
  • Skipping etcd upgrade can cause version incompatibility
  • Not taking etcd snapshot means no rollback path

docs.title: Verification
docs.text: bash kubectl get nodes kubectl version --short etcdctl --endpoints=https://127.0.0.1:2379 endpoint health --cluster cat kubespray/VERSION

docs.title: Symptoms
docs.text:
• vault status reports Sealed: true.
  • vault login returns a permission error.
  • A secret is not found at an expected path.
  • Secret delivery to a workload stops.
  • A certificate is not renewed.
  • The audit log stops receiving entries.

docs.title: Likely causes
docs.text: Cause Discriminator The cluster is sealed after a restart or an unclean shutdown vault status shows Sealed: true The token expired vault token lookup fails, or a 403 with "permission denied" The token lacks the policy vault token capabilities <path> The secret is at a different mount or version vault secrets list -detailed The application is using a stale cached token The workload has not restarted since the rotation The seal keys are unavailable Fewer than the threshold of shares are held The audit device's disk is full or its host is down vault audit list, and check the audit device host The Vault node is not the leader vault status shows HA Enabled: true with leader: false

docs.title: Diagnostic commands
docs.text:
# Status and seal state
vault status
vault status -format=json

# Leader and cluster members
vault operator raft list-peers
vault operator raft autopilot state

# Sealed and unseal
vault operator unseal <key-share>
vault operator seal
vault operator unseal -status

# Token
vault token lookup
vault token capabilities secret/apps/payments/db
vault token create -policy=app-payments -ttl=1h -renewable=false

# Secrets
vault secrets list -detailed
vault kv get -format=json secret/apps/payments/db
vault kv metadata get secret/apps/payments/db

# Auth methods
vault auth list
vault write auth/kubernetes/login role=app jwt="$JWT"

# Audit
vault audit list
vault audit list -detailed

# Runtime
vault operator raft autopilot configuration
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8200/v1/sys/health | jq

docs.title: Expected healthy state
docs.text:
Sealed          false
HA Enabled      true
Key Shares      5
Key Threshold   3
Last Half Rotation Time   ...
Next Half Rotation Time   ...

vault status shows Sealed: false, HA Enabled: true, and one leader among the peers.

docs.title: Sealed cluster
docs.text:
# With the required number of shares
vault operator unseal <share-1>
vault operator unseal <share-2>
vault operator unseal <share-3>
vault status

If the shares are lost, the cluster cannot be unsealed with them. Options, in order: use the root token with vault operator generate-root (needs a quorum of shares, so it does not help if the shares are lost), or restore from the raft snapshot (secrets-management/recovery/restore.md). There is no other path.

docs.title: Permission denied
docs.text:
# What the token can actually do
vault token capabilities secret/apps/payments/db
vault token lookup -format=json | jq '.data.policies'

# Read the policy
vault policy read app-payments

Common causes: - The policy path does not match the actual path. secret/apps/payments/* does not match secret/apps/payments (no trailing wildcard). - The token was created with a policy that has since been changed. - The namespace binding on the Kubernetes role does not include this service account. - The policy grants create but not read, or update but not read.

docs.title: A secret is not found
docs.text:
vault secrets list -detailed        # confirm the mount and the KV version
vault kv get secret/apps/payments/db
vault kv list secret/apps/payments/

For KV v2, the API path is secret/data/<path> while the CLI takes secret/<path>. A path written for v1 fails against v2 with "no handler for route".

docs.title: Secret delivery stopped
docs.text:
# The injector
kubectl -n <ns> get pods -l vault.hashicorp.com/agent-inject=true
kubectl -n <ns> logs <pod> -c vault-agent-init -c vault-agent

# The External Secrets Operator
kubectl get externalsecrets -A
kubectl describe externalsecret <name> -n <ns>
kubectl -n external-secrets logs deploy/external-secrets --tail=100

Common causes: - The Vault token the pod uses expired and the injector could not renew it. - The service account token bound to the Vault role was deleted or recreated with a different name. - The Vault auth method's token_reviewer_jwt expired. - The Vault role's TTL is shorter than the pod's lifetime and renewal is disabled.

docs.title: Certificate not renewed
docs.text:
kubectl get certificaterequest -A
kubectl describe certificate <name> -n <ns>
kubectl -n cert-manager logs deploy/cert-manager -c cert-manager --tail=100
vault write pki/issue/<role> common_name=test.internal ttl=1h

Common causes: - The issuer cannot reach Vault. - The Vault PKI role's max_ttl is shorter than the certificate's requested TTL, so cert-manager cannot renew with the requested duration. - The CA is expired or its intermediate has expired.

docs.title: Audit device stopped
docs.text:
vault audit list
vault audit list -detailed
df -h <audit-path>

An audit device that cannot write is disabled by Vault. Check the disk on the audit device host and re-enable it.

docs.title: Risks
docs.text:
• vault operator seal requires the same quorum to unseal. Do not seal a cluster casually.
  • vault policy write affects every token bound to that policy immediately. Review the diff before applying.
  • Deleting an auth method or a policy breaks every consumer of it.
  • vault operator raft snapshot save on a cluster with a large backend takes time; a snapshot taken during heavy writes may not be consistent.

docs.title: Verification after remediation
docs.text:
vault status
vault read database/creds/<role>          # dynamic credential issuance
vault write pki/issue/<role> common_name=test.internal ttl=1h
vault write auth/kubernetes/login role=<role> jwt="$JWT"
kubectl -n <ns> get externalsecret

Then re-run acceptance tests S-01, S-02, S-03, and D-06.
